note: LLM red team (Sonnet role runs + checker). Used only to find behaviours the rule model misses; not used in any statistical result.

kept.behaviour: Cross-field triage of shared preparer time. With the owner gone, the remaining preparer has one pool of preparation time for every application (HSIP, Prop L, general fund/CIP, other signal and safety grants). APS has no capital-plan category and no duty to apply, so it is the first task bumped when another application falls in the same window. The task goes to MISSED, not DEFLECTED.
kept.parameter: w_crowd (crowd-out logit weight) applied to an exogenous competing workload L_comp(t); optional hard cap K_app
kept.range: w_crowd U(0, 3), default 0 (off); L_comp U(0, 1.5) competing applications per window; or K_app in {1, 2, 3} with 3 = no constraint. Active only while F-h vacancy (t_vac) is on
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start logistic: add −w_crowd·L_comp(t) during the vacancy (or an admission test rank ≤ K_app before the p_start draw; a failed test means MISSED). Today each field has its own independent task and strain(t) is the same for all fields, so starts cannot crowd each other out.
kept.evidence: Not covered: D3.1 'one task per field', and F-h/F-i change only owner, q_drop and K_crew. Context checked in 01: no accessibility category in the CIP (l.155, CIP25 p.4); grants 'prefer expansion over maintenance' (l.149, CIPpol p.11); funding 'urgent needs by phase / readiness' (l.154, CIPpol p.6); the policy does not require applying for funds (l.115, POL10 p.2, 'no duty' is inference); scoring has no cost or feasibility term (TOOL p.2-5); one associate engineer scores all requests (l.106, 'only one' is inference). Nearest precedent: EP17 hardware money went to about 98 controllers rather than APS (l.126, OCT25 p.7), but that is money, not preparer time. The HSIP C13 deadline 2026-11-02 is verified (01 l.219). No document shows APS being triaged against another application during a vacancy.

kept.behaviour: Stale carry-forward package. Instead of rebuilding the HSIP package, the caretaker re-files the previous cycle's package or the CIP line as written (same intersections and carriers, old crash window and old unit price). Preparation is faster, so fewer windows are MISSED. But there is no BCR re-sort, no split by measure union and no eligibility repair, so more F-a/F-b/F-c failures follow.
kept.parameter: q_stale (probability a package prepared during the vacancy is a carry-forward) with m_carry (D_prep multiplier)
kept.range: q_stale U(0, 0.8), default 0; m_carry U(0.3, 0.7); on a hit the package is the previous instance set unchanged, and its BCR is recomputed on current costs (u0 / g_cost drift) with no repack
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 packaging steps 2-5 (BCR sort, measure-union split, 5.0 gate repair), replaced by the previous set on a hit; D3.1 PREPARING duration D_prep + (m−1)·δ_split multiplied by m_carry. Active only while F-h vacancy is on.
kept.evidence: Not covered: D3.3 rebuilds the package each round, and F-b allows repacking only as an option. 01 l.420: SFMTA's own SG142 (pure APS, $488,144) is ineligible in C13 as written and exceeds the $360k cap (verified), which shows a line carried unrepackaged. 01 l.140: SG142/SG143 'HSIP C13/C14 – EST' lines are already programmed (verified), a ready template. 01 l.119: unit floor $20k→$40k, about 9-10%/yr (verified), which is why stale costs fail. 01 l.549/l.224: the HSIP C12 money planned for SG136 was never applied for (verified). None of this shows reuse caused by a vacancy.

kept.behaviour: Stop-gap cover for the vacant role. An acting designee, an on-call grant consultant, or a limited-term post funded from capital or grant money takes over application preparation. A headcount freeze does not necessarily block this. Capacity comes back after a procurement or onboarding lag, not only when t_vac ends. One variant (run 4) allows cover only if some APS money already exists, which makes the vacancy length depend on funding.
kept.parameter: q_cover (probability cover is found during the vacancy) with t_onboard (lag)
kept.range: q_cover U(0, 0.7), default 0; t_onboard U(2, 9) months; variant: q_cover = 0 unless A_local > 0 or an APPROVED instance exists; optional cost c_consult U($30k, $120k) per package, booked in cost_by_actor
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-h recovery path (owner restored at min(t_vac, t_onboard) when cover is found) and F-i recovery; D10 t_vac row becomes state-dependent. The outsourcing in F-e/F-i and sw_consult apply only to design and construction, not to application preparation.
kept.evidence: Not covered: F-h recovers only by refilling after t_vac; F-i's outsourcing is 'same as F-e' (construction contracting); sw_consult is consultant design for the CON deadline. 01 l.104: 8 of 21 electrician posts sit on the project-support fund, 'expected to be recovered from capital projects' (ASO27 p.123; verified, though run 4 cited l.107 by mistake). 01 l.105: the 9145 eligible list grew to 41 during the freeze (2025-05) (verified), but that list is for electricians, not grant writers. 01 l.152: 89 vacancies deleted, 'no new headcount' (BB27 p.4-6, verified). No document shows a consultant or acting designee preparing applications.

kept.behaviour: Loss of tacit knowledge. The departed owner held the scoring tool, the candidate list, the know-how for using SI02 as a carrier, and the SFCTA/Caltrans contacts. Until someone relearns this, every package takes longer to prepare, during the vacancy and for a learning period after the post is filled or covered.
kept.parameter: kappa_know (multiplier on D_prep) with t_learn
kept.range: kappa_know U(1.0, 2.5), default 1 (off); applied during the vacancy and for t_learn U(3, 12) months after refill or cover
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 preparation duration D_prep + (m−1)·δ_split. Today D_prep is a single U(1, 6) draw that does not depend on staffing.
kept.evidence: Not covered: F-h changes only the owner tier and q_drop, and D_prep (D10) does not depend on staffing. 01 l.419: SI02 as an APS carrier rests only on an author interview, with no public Caltrans ruling (verified), so the know-how is oral (inference). 01 l.106: one associate engineer scores all requests ('only one person' is inference, verified). No document gives a knowledge-loss rate. Runs 2 and 3 also linked a person-dependent sw_si02; that part is left out because D3.6 treats SI02_carrier as a global uncertainty switch.

kept.behaviour: Administrative obligations lapse. The same person keeps SF eligible and funded projects alive: LRSP renewal, red-flag remediation, PIF and E-76 paperwork, the 5-year extension. While the post is vacant these slow down or are dropped, which is a second route from vacancy to lost funding that does not go through p_start.
kept.parameter: nu_vac (duration multiplier) with q_miss_admin
kept.range: nu_vac U(1.0, 2.5) on t_lrsp, t_fix, t_pif, t_dsg while vacant; default 1; q_miss_admin U(0, 0.3) per milestone, a miss becoming a red flag
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 LRSP continuous-state rule and red-flag remediation (t_fix, F-c); D3.4 HSIP milestone nodes (t_pif, t_dsg; F-d red flags). Linked to F-h vacancy.
kept.evidence: Not covered: t_lrsp, t_fix, t_pif and t_dsg (D3.3, D3.4, D10) are fixed draws; F-h touches only owner and PREPARING. 01 l.106 (one associate engineer, verified) and 01 l.583 (an approved vacancy takes 6-9 months to fill, citywide average 8 months, verified). No document shows lapsed paperwork.

dropped.behaviour: Silent window miss from lost calendar knowledge, modelled as an awareness gate p_unaware before p_start (run 3)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.1 together with D3.5 F-h. When the owner drops a tier, p_start falls, and the result is the same: the task stays IDLE and the window passes unused. A multiplicative gate cannot be told apart from a lower β_own·owner term in any model output, because no rule depends on whether outsiders see the miss.

dropped.behaviour: Vacancy cited as the stated reason for deflection, with a longer wait r until strain_end (run 2)
dropped.reason: Covered by the D3.1 DEFLECTED branch: the stated reason ('cost / no funds' vs 'no staff') has no consequence in the model, and p_deflect is already U(0.5, 0.95) in M-A and M-D (D10). Switching deflection on in M-B would break the D3.2 mechanism matrix, which keeps the mechanisms separable. No source for the reason (01 §2.1 shows only cost / no-funds replies, MDC26 p.4-6, p.8).

dropped.behaviour: Reframing the APS request into an SGR or street-safety category, with leakage/dilution of the funded line (run 1)
dropped.reason: Not triggered by the vacancy or the freeze, so it is outside this scenario. It also overlaps D3.6 PW6 (APS written into the existing SG017 replacement line) and PW5. Needs at least two linked parameters (q_reframe plus an approval uplift plus d_dilute), not one switch.

dropped.behaviour: Reclassifying Signal Shop labour to capital codes to keep installs moving without an application (run 2)
dropped.reason: Not an A2 application behaviour and not specific to the vacancy. It overlaps D3.5 F-k q_dir (SG000 / commissioner's 10%) and the D3.6 PW5 b_hw maintenance add-on. Needs a switch plus three parameters (q_reclass, a_reclass, q_audit). 01 l.158 (work-order restructuring option, $2.5M) explicitly does not name the Signal Shop, so the support is indirect.

kept.behaviour: Decouple APS from the C13 carrier application. When time is short or the bundle's BCR is near 5.0, A2 submits the SG015 carrier package alone (or prepares it first and the APS-bearing package only if time remains). APS then goes back to the waiting pool, to local money (SG142 local line / A_local), or to a post-award scope add. Merges the post-award add, the non-participating carve-out, decoupled fallback, the cost-line carving and the deadline triage/ordering proposals.
kept.parameter: aps_in_app ∈ {0 = APS in the HSIP application (current rule), 1 = carrier alone, APS to local / post-award}, chosen with probability p_decouple when D_prep+(m−1)·δ_split exceeds the time left or the package BCR is within theta_bcr_margin of 5.0; companions q_local_ok (local money approved for the APS share) and q_addon_fail / t_addon for the post-award branch
kept.range: p_decouple U(0, 1) (0 reproduces the current model); theta_bcr_margin U(0.5, 2.0); q_local_ok U(0.3, 0.9); q_addon_fail U(0.2, 0.8); t_addon U(3, 12) months
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 route A 'BCR denominator uses full project cost' and packing step ④; D3.6 PW1 start (SG015 + APS bundled); D3.1 deadline step (which instance becomes MISSED); D3.4 adds a post-award add branch. F-g 'unbind: APS goes local' exists only after a partner delay or cancellation, not as a choice made before submission.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.442 shows SG015 ($1.1M) and SG142 ($488,144) on separate CIP rows, both 'CaltransFHWAHSIPCycle13(2027) - EST', FY28. 01 §2.1 decision rule 'all new signals and major upgrades install APS; installing with existing works is cheapest' (MDC23 p.6; MDC26 p.7). 01 l.637 (C4): 'eligible portion local pays 10%, ineligible portion fully self-paid'. 01 §2.4: non-safety items ≤10% of construction (LAPG ch.9 p.4). No document shows SFMTA actually decoupling or carving out APS. Whether APS hardware can legally sit outside the BCR cost is unverified.

kept.behaviour: Belief-driven carrier choice with a pre-submission query. A2 acts on its belief about whether SI02 counts as an APS carrier and may ask Caltrans Local Assistance before spending prep time. Depending on the answer it proceeds, keeps only safe carriers (SI18PB / SI22PB / SI07), or drops APS from C13.
kept.parameter: p_belief_si02 (A2's prior that SI02 is usable), plus q_ask (probability of asking before PREPARING), t_reply, and a_reply (probability the answer matches the true sw_si02 state)
kept.range: p_belief_si02 U(0, 1); q_ask U(0, 0.8) (0 reproduces the current model); t_reply U(0.5, 4) months; a_reply U(0.6, 1.0)
kept.rule_modified: D3.6 sw_si02 / SI02_carrier (currently only a world switch with no actor belief); D3.3 route A carrier selection ('highest-BCR combination'); D3.1 adds a branch before IDLE → PREPARING; O2 gains an A2 belief variable
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.419 (§3.1 hard facts): SI02 as an APS carrier rests on 'author interview (primary), no public Caltrans determination'. 01 l.417: the C12 0/3 result had 'no written rule'; the first written statement is the 2025-12 advisory minutes. 01 l.220: C12 pure-APS 0/3. 01 l.664 lists this as an open question. No document shows SFMTA staff asking Caltrans.

kept.behaviour: Paper-funding placeholder. The ineligible SG142 line stays in the CIP with its HSIP 'EST' source, or is rolled to C14 by relabelling, instead of being declared unfunded. The line works as a 'funded in plan' answer to advocates and oversight. That stretches deflection and lowers p_start in the next window.
kept.parameter: p_placeholder: probability the plan line is kept after a MISSED/REJECTED or no-application cycle. While held, pressure(t) is multiplied by (1 − ρ_ph) for t_ph months.
kept.range: p_placeholder U(0, 0.8) (0 reproduces the current model); ρ_ph U(0, 0.5); t_ph U(12, 36) months
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch / pressure(t) decay and the post-MISSED reset; D3.2 matrix (M-A, M-D columns). D3.5 F-a to F-m have no failure where a plan line masks a missed application.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.224: SG136 'APS FY25' $1.0M was planned from HSIP C12, and no SF APS application appears among the 330 C12 applications (CIP25 l.2308–2312; C12apps l.317). 01 l.140: SG142 $488,144 'HSIP C13 – EST'. 01 l.420: SG142 is ineligible as written. 01 §2.1: SG136 has no money row in FY27-31 (labelled inference, strong). 01 l.83: the 'say no money / not applied' loop (the link is labelled inference). That the line works as a shield that lowers pressure has no document.

kept.behaviour: Widening the carrier scope inside C13. A2 adds pending C-type intersections outside the five named SG015 corridors (more 8→12-inch heads or backplates) to the C13 carrier application, instead of waiting until the C14 repack.
kept.parameter: n_carrier_expand: number of extra pending C intersections admitted to the PW1 candidate set at C13. Each adds δ_split prep time and c_12in/c_bp carrier cost. Companion q_scope: rejection risk for scope not matching the programmed project.
kept.range: n_carrier_expand integer 0–8 (0 reproduces the current model), applied only if prep time fits before the deadline; q_scope U(0, 0.3)
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 packing step ① ('PW1 starts only on SG015 corridors'); D3.6 PW1 start and the '< 2 intersections' signpost (currently widened only at C14); D3.1 PREPARING duration
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.444: SG015 is limited to five named corridors (Alemany, Outer Mission, 25th, Brotherhood, Sunset) and gives priority to arterials 'where visibility could be improved using existing signal poles' (CIP27m l.2441–2446). The inference is about 1 unfunded C intersection. 01 l.432: corridor candidates join at corridor design. Run 3's claim that the scope is 'set by staff, not a board' is not supported, because 01 l.442 cites an SFMTA Board CIP memo. No document shows a pre-deadline scope widening. With the C13 deadline on 2026-11-02 (01 §2.4), a CIP amendment within a week is doubtful, so the parameter should apply to application content, not to CIP wording.

kept.behaviour: Strategic waiting for an APS-only rule change. Because the advisory committee said it 'will study again', A2 does not prepare an APS-bearing HSIP application this cycle and holds the APS line for a later window. The wait belief fades if no rule signal appears.
kept.parameter: w_wait: a term subtracted from the HSIP-field p_start logit (−w_wait·wait(t)), decaying each window that brings no relaxation
kept.range: w_wait U(0, 1.5) logit units (0 = control); decay factor per window U(0.3, 0.9)
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start formula for the HSIP field only. D3.3 and D11 exclude the rule change itself, not the actor's waiting on it, so the model's 'no rule relaxation' stays intact.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.207 (§2.4): 2025-12 advisory committee replied 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects' and 'will study again' (caltrans-hsip-meeting-minutes-20251211 p.3). 01 §2.1: the policy does not require applying for funds (POL10 p.2; 'no duty' is itself labelled inference). That SFMTA staff wait because of this has no document.

dropped.behaviour: Post-award scope add (run 1), non-participating APS cost carve-out (run 2), decoupled carrier-alone fallback (run 2), cost-line carving aps_in_app (run 4)
dropped.reason: Duplicates, merged into kept item 1 (decouple APS from the carrier application).

dropped.behaviour: Risk-hedged preparation ordering (run 1) and final-week triage of preparer capacity (run 3)
dropped.reason: Merged into kept item 1. In the PW1 C13 situation the only competing 'clean' instance is SG015 alone, so ordering by risk gives the same carrier-alone submission. D3.1 already marks late instances MISSED through D_prep+(m−1)·δ_split. The ordering refinement does not justify a separate slot under the 5-item cap.

dropped.behaviour: Informal pre-clearance with Caltrans Local Assistance (run 1)
dropped.reason: Duplicate, merged into kept item 2 (belief-driven SI02 carrier choice with query).

dropped.behaviour: Paper funding via the SG142 line as a deflection shield (run 1)
dropped.reason: Duplicate, merged into kept item 3 (placeholder).

dropped.behaviour: Scope-stretch of SG015 corridor wording (run 2)
dropped.reason: Duplicate, merged into kept item 4 (carrier scope expansion inside C13).

dropped.behaviour: Strategic abstention waiting for a rule change (run 3, sw_wait_rule)
dropped.reason: Duplicate, merged into kept item 5 (w_wait).

dropped.behaviour: Rushed or thin submission at the deadline (run 2, p_rush / q_rush_rej)
dropped.reason: Proposed by one run only, with no document support (01 l.587 is about the LRSP running in parallel, not about thin applications). Cut by the 5-item cap. Kept items have more runs proposing them or better-sourced context.

dropped.behaviour: Strategic BCR-assumption tuning to clear 5.0 (run 4, bcr_tuning)
dropped.reason: Proposed by one run only. Cut by the 5-item cap. D10 already spans Y_win / L_rule / f_aff as draws, and D3.3 treats f_aff=1 as an upper bound, so a scan partly covers the range. Whether the applicant can freely choose the crash window is not verified in 01. The citation (QA13 Q65, 01 §2.4) is real but supports only the threshold, not the tuning.

kept.behaviour: Descope and substitute inside the funded local batch. At the design-complete node, if the overrun goes beyond contingency, A2 sends the dig-heavy sites (new conduit or ramp) back to the pool and spends the freed money on the cheapest no-dig C-type pool sites, instead of the current top-up-or-terminate draw. Substitute sites get a fresh t_des and their own overrun draw. Effect: more sites per dollar now, costly sites drift to never_served.
kept.parameter: p_descope (probability of choosing descope/swap over a top-up request); optional d_floor = minimum share of the original batch kept. p_descope = 0 gives back the current model
kept.range: U(0, 0.8); sensitivity points {0, 0.5, 0.9}; d_floor 0.5–1
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-f: new step between 'beyond contingency' and the q_topup draw. Also §D3.4 local-batch site selection: add a cheapest-first back-fill. Not covered today: F-f only has contingency → q_topup → TERMINATED/back to pool, and §D3.3 packing picks sites only at intake.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01: §2.2 says SG142 is 'about 22 sites, no excavation, all built by Signal Shop' (CIP27m l.292–294, l.2511). §2.1 says the easy sites are already done and the rest are harder and costlier (NA24 §1.4). §2.1 says the rest of the list is 'selected based on funding' (MDC26 p.8). §2.1 has the claim that not touching the existing ramp is 'five times faster' (MDC26t; stated, untested). §3.2 l.446 says SG017 allows new APS where the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition. All of these lines are real. No document shows anyone swapping sites after design, so that step is inferred.

kept.behaviour: Move the ramp or conduit part of the overrun to another budget, mainly the Public Works curb-ramp program or a partner signal or paving project. SFMTA keeps only the APS hardware and conduit cost. This turns a funding gap into a wait for someone else's schedule.
kept.parameter: phi_shift (share of the ramp/conduit add-on moved off the batch ledger); companion t_shift delay
kept.range: phi_shift U(0, 0.7), applied only where a live ramp or partner project exists. t_shift U(6, 36) months, taken from the Contract 35/36 durations (could reuse the t_partner family)
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-f: gap = actual − plan·(1+κ_cont) − phi_shift·(ramp+conduit add-on), computed before q_topup. The site then waits on a parent event, as with D3.4 merge-into-project or F-g. Today, merge-into-project (PW4/D3.4) is chosen only at intake, so this is not a duplicate.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.11: 'DPW designs ramps reserving for future APS, but ramp construction does not trigger APS; APS is MTA's business' (MDC26t). Ramp budget is $4.0M in FY26 and $8.1M/$12.2M requested for FY27/28. Contract 35 slipped about 8 years (OCT25 p.27). C35/C36 ran 6–9.5 years. §2.1 says conduit and ramp are each about $200k (MDC26 p.4–5). Counter-evidence in §2.1: the senior engineer cites the 'litigation environment' as the reason to insist that curb work is done together with APS (MDC26t), and DPW treats APS as MTA's job. So a split is possible but would meet resistance. Nothing documents an APS cost split being made after an overrun.

kept.behaviour: Hold the top-up request until a funding window opens, and pick the channel. A2 does not file at the discovery moment. They wait for the next annual CIP or local cycle, a 5YPP amendment, the SG000 reserve or the Director's 10% authority, or fold the gap into a phased or broader ask. The site sits design-complete and outside the crew queue, while the 60-month clock and red flags keep running.
kept.parameter: t_topup_wait (months from discovery to the request decision; can snap to the next window), with switch sw_cycle_gate. Optional: approval chance by channel
kept.range: U(0, 12) months, or snap to the next local window (02 O3: opens 1 Jan, decided 1 Jul). sw_cycle_gate ∈ {0,1}, where 0 is the current instant q_topup
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-f top-up branch, which is a single instant q_topup today. t_pause exists only in F-e. F-k uses the Director's 10% and SG000 only as a starting source, not as an overrun channel.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.2: 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (CIPpol p.6). Capital revenue is about $246M lower and 'not enough to fund all approved projects' (CIPpol p.5, p.20). The board wants diversions to be one-off and spread out (CIPpol p.18, p.21). The Director may adjust up to 10% without the Board (RES l.22, l.82). SG000 is $1.6M + $0.5M (CIP27m). §2.3: the D4 5YPP revision took 3–4 months. Two problems: (1) the SFCTA '13th St $2.7M top-up' precedent that runs 1–2 cite through F-f (02 F-f says 'ledger §2.11') does not appear in 01 §2.11 or anywhere in 01, so it is unverified. (2) The Jan–Jul local window comes from 02 O3 and is marked inferred there; run 4 attributed it to 01 §2.2, which does not contain it. Nothing documents deliberate waiting on an overrun.

kept.behaviour: Relabel the overrun as fundable state-of-good-repair or hardware-replacement work. A2 records the conduit or pole work on existing (C-type) sites as SGR or life-extending capital, or adds it to a hardware-replacement work order, so that SGR or EP17 hardware money pays instead of the empty APS line. This is not new money: other signal SGR work is delayed.
kept.parameter: q_relabel (probability a C-type overrun site can be recoded; covers a share of the gap). N-type sites get 0
kept.range: q_relabel U(0.1, 0.6); share of gap covered U(0.1, 0.5); pool capped jointly with PW5's b_hw; optional delay to other SGR work U(3, 12) months
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-f gap source order becomes contingency → relabel pool → q_topup. Shares the account of §D3.3 PW5 b_hw. Today PW5 b_hw is triggered only by the λ_hw hardware event, not by an overrun.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.2: the FY27–31 CIP plans to widen 'capital investment' to cover maintenance that extends life by 5+ years (CIPpol p.10). Signals are among the most degraded assets and SGR money is 'extremely limited' (CIPpol p.10). The 2025-02 budget option 'restructure work orders so they count as capital' (sfmta-media-41700 p.9, p.17) does not name Signal Shop. §2.1: EP17 hardware money of $1M went to about 98 firewall-flawed controllers, although the 2023 PIF listed APS as eligible (OCT25 p.7), which shows SGR priorities compete. All lines are real. Their use for APS overruns is not documented. Run 4's ADA/street-safety relabel (q_topup_ramp) is folded into this item and into the cost-shift item: the $125M/10-yr ADA right-of-way pay-go (§2.6, CP-I p.4) and the curb-ramp MDC letters (§2.7) are real, but they point to the DPW ramp pot.

kept.behaviour: Park the designed site in a HELD state instead of terminating it, and use the finished design as a readiness argument in the next 5YPP or CIP window. The site keeps its design and does not go back to the pool as a new site. It re-enters with a higher approval chance until the design goes stale.
kept.parameter: b_ready (boost to approval probability when a HELD design-complete site re-enters). Switch p_hold or sw_hold, where 0 is the current TERMINATED path
kept.range: b_ready U(0, 0.2); t_hold 6–30 months; design stale limit 36–84 months (inferred)
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-f 'no top-up' branch and the §D3.4 termination clause, which today cancels all events and returns a plain site to the pool with no memory of its design. F-e's t_pause covers only the outsourcing branch.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3: the Prop L 5YPP score gives readiness 5 of 31 points (EP17-5YPP p.12–13). Also §2.3: construction allocation requires 95% drawings, environmental review and permits (SP p.19–23). §2.2 has the CIP rule 'fund in phases (raise readiness)' (CIPpol p.6). These lines are real. The step from them to 'a shelved design wins a later bid' is inference.

dropped.behaviour: Delayed disclosure of the overrun (t_hide): keep the design open (for example at 90%) so the gap is not recorded until a window opens or a cheaper scope is found (run 2)
dropped.reason: There is no source at all; run 2 itself calls it speculative, and the nearest line (§2.1, responding to advocates with 'no money') is about framing, not hiding a cost. dropped.behaviour: Portfolio crowd-out by A2's own non-APS grant applications (run4 m_crowd × n_competing)
dropped.reason: Mostly covered: R_other (D3.3, D10) already takes HSIP cap dollars, and strain(t) (D3.1/D3.2 M-B) already lowers p_start for prep capacity. n_competing has no data source. A citation is misused: 'one associate engineer scores all applications' (01 §2.1) is about scoring requests on the APS list, not about preparing grants. One run only.

dropped.behaviour: Paper commitment specifics: listed_unfunded flag and q_stale (run1)
dropped.reason: Merged into the kept placation branch (p_placate). The extra flags and q_stale are more than one parameter, and the D4 gap output is kept only as an optional add-on.

dropped.behaviour: Risk-averse BCR submission margin (run1 bcr_margin)
dropped.reason: Merged into delivery-risk aversion (m_flag) as an alternative way to implement the same motive. Not kept as a separate item.

dropped.behaviour: Capital-coded work order as a new APS funding path (run2 b_reclass, run4 q_capitalize/a_cap)
dropped.reason: Overlaps PW5's maintenance allowance b_hw (D3.6) and PW6. No document names APS as a reclassification target. The selection-bias half is kept as w_labor; the funding-path half needs extra parameters and is dropped.

kept.behaviour: Finance releases discretion only when an APS request is live. The 10% director adjustment and the SG000 reserve go to APS only in a month when a live, ready APS request exists (a PREPARING or SUBMITTED instance). While the owner post is vacant nobody files that request, so q_dir cannot reach APS. Merges run1 #1 (sponsor gate), run2 #2 (hold-and-wait), run4 #1 (match-first).
kept.parameter: sw_dir_live_request (0/1). If 1, q_dir_eff = q_dir x 1[live APS instance this month]; if 0, the current F-k is unchanged.
kept.range: switch 0/1 (0 = current model); q_dir keeps U(0,0.8)
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-k (line 230): q_dir changes from an unconditional draw to one that depends on the state of the D3.1 task.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.2: l.154 CIPpol p.6 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (verified); l.149 CIPpol p.11 'most flexible money goes to match' (verified); l.139 SG000 $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28 (verified); l.156 director <=10% without board (verified). No document says discretion is withheld when no request or sponsor exists. 02 F-k currently gives q_dir as an independent probability with no link to F-h.

kept.behaviour: Finance holds the match commitment. While no owner is named, finance will not commit the 10% local match for an HSIP instance. If the commitment is not issued by the deadline, the instance becomes MISSED, which is a new cause besides D_prep running out.
kept.parameter: q_match_hold: the probability that finance holds the match commitment while F-h vacancy is active. An unmet commitment at the deadline gives MISSED.
kept.range: U(0, 0.7); 0 = current model
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.1 PREPARING to SUBMIT transition (adds a gate) and §D3.3 local match (line 190 only states 'local match 10%' as a cost share).
kept.evidence: 01 §2.4 l.203 (QA13 Q14, Q59): 90% reimbursement, 10% local match, staff hours can be soft match (verified). l.149 CIPpol p.11: flexible money goes to match (verified). Withholding a match letter is undocumented. Soft match is not in 02 at all, so it could later be added as a bypass share. Run4 cited this as 's2.12'; the source is actually §2.4.

kept.behaviour: A vacancy lasts as long as the freeze unless the post is grant-funded. Under the hiring freeze, finance grants refill exemptions only to grant-reimbursable posts. APS has no live grant, so the vacancy lasts until the freeze ends instead of an independent t_vac. This merges run1 #3 (exemption follows funding) with run1 #2 (frozen post's funding swept, so the vacancy is longer).
kept.parameter: sw_vac_freeze (0/1). If 1 and no APS-linked grant or line is live, t_vac = max(t_vac, strain_end - quit date).
kept.range: switch 0/1 (0 = current independent t_vac U(3,18))
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-h (t_vac, line 227) linked to F-i strain_end (line 228); these are currently independent draws.
kept.evidence: 01 §2.1 l.105 (41 eligible in 2025-05, during freeze) and l.104 (8/21 posts on project-support fund, 38%) are real, but both concern 9145 electricians, not the APS engineer post. They do not show an exemption rule for the owner post. 01 l.549: hiring slowed 2024-07 and non-essential hiring frozen 2024-10 (sfmta-media-41700 l.118-120). The exemption rule itself is undocumented.

kept.behaviour: APS competes with overruns for one discretion pool. Finance uses the 10% director adjustment first to top up projects that are already committed (overruns, outsourcing premium, partner shortfalls), so that no committed project loses funding. APS, with no champion, draws on whatever remains.
kept.parameter: w_drain: the weight of same-year top-up draws (F-e and F-f q_topup approvals) on the shared pool. q_dir_eff = q_dir x max(0, 1 - w_drain x pool_used_share).
kept.range: U(0, 1); 0 = current independent q_dir
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-k coupled with F-e and F-f q_topup (lines 224-225, 379); these currently draw independently.
kept.evidence: 01 §2.2 l.156 (<=10% ~ $65M director adjustment), l.157 CIPpol p.18, p.21 (board: diversions one-time, spread 'so no project loses funding'), l.154 (fulfil contract obligations first), l.139 SG000. All verified. How the pool is divided among claimants is undocumented.

kept.behaviour: Finance pays for readiness instead of the owner. It holds the request until the next programming window, then funds only a readiness step (application prep or design support). This partly restores owner capacity without a hire, at the cost of waiting for the window.
kept.parameter: ready_gain: the share of the F-h owner downgrade restored at the next window, released with probability q_ready.
kept.range: ready_gain U(0, 0.7); q_ready U(0, 0.5); both 0 = current model
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-h recovery path (line 227 currently recovers only by hiring after t_vac), feeding beta_own in p_start (§D3.1).
kept.evidence: 01 §2.2 l.154 CIPpol p.6 'fund in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' (verified). The next 5YPP window, autumn 2027 to 2028, is in 01 l.69 and l.192 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46) (verified). Using readiness money to substitute for a vacant owner is undocumented.

dropped.behaviour: Labour recoding to capital: finance books Signal Shop hours as capital and steers crew to chargeable or externally funded work (run2 #1, run3 #3, run4 #2).
dropped.reason: For the model this is already covered. Lower K_crew under the freeze is D3.2 strain(t) and F-i (line 228). D3.4 (line 205) lets only funded intersections enter the crew queue, so the 'unfunded APS installs' that would be displaced do not exist there, and run2's opposite claim (more K_crew) has no new cash. In the model it reduces to a K_crew multiplier that is already there. Citation check: 01 l.158 is real but says paint and sign shop, not Signal Shop; l.159 is real.

dropped.behaviour: Permanent K_crew ratchet after a swept post (K_loss part of run1 #2).
dropped.reason: It conflates the APS engineer (owner) post with 9145 electrician crew capacity. 01 l.104 (8/21 on project-support fund) concerns electricians. The duration part is merged into the kept item sw_vac_freeze.

dropped.behaviour: Budget office redirects APS requests as riders on corridor or signal projects (run2 #3, p_redirect).
dropped.reason: Embedding delivery is already the PW4 per-intersection allocation and the embedded route (02 §D3.6 line 244, D3.4). The model has no budget-office request event outside the D3.1 DEFLECTED branch, so the trigger cannot be attached without a new actor. It was also cut to stay within 5. Citation: 01 l.265 CP-T p.11 is verified, but it sits in §2.6, not §2.11 as cited.

dropped.behaviour: Finance parks responsibility back on the vacant engineering unit (run4 #4, r_vac_mult, p_deflect_vac).
dropped.reason: Already covered by 02 §D3.1 DEFLECTED (line 124, and the note that neighbouring nodes never take over a deflected task): deflected pressure already leaves no effect, so a reverse leg or a longer r changes nothing. Sensitivity to p_deflect is already swept, U(0.5,0.95) (line 342).

dropped.behaviour: Reserve lapse and decay of unspent SG000 (reserve_lapse_rate, lambda_sweep in run1 #1 and run2 #2).
dropped.reason: Merged as a duplicate into the kept F-k item (sw_dir_live_request), so that item stays a single switch. A time-decaying pool would need a pool state the model lacks; it overlaps the kept w_drain coupling.

kept.behaviour: Sweep of unobligated local APS placeholder money after an HSIP miss or lapse: once an APS-carrying HSIP application fails, is rejected or is never filed, finance cuts or reassigns the unobligated EST local APS dollars (SG143 $570k general-fund line, the APS-usable share of SG000 or director discretion) toward SGR, grant-ready projects or the operating gap. Local fallback availability decays over time instead of being one fixed draw.
kept.parameter: q_sweep (annual hazard that an unobligated local APS line is cut or reassigned after an HSIP failure or lapse), with sweep fraction f_sweep
kept.range: q_sweep U(0, 0.5)/yr (runs proposed 0-0.4 and 0-0.5); f_sweep U(0.25, 1). Note that 01 l.157 (board: transfers 'one-time', 'spread out so no project loses funding') argues for keeping f_sweep below 1 as a sensitivity. q_sweep = 0 reproduces the current model.
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-k (q_dir becomes q_dir·exp(-q_sweep·years since miss)) and D10 A_local; the local fallback steps of D3.6 PW1, PW2 and PW6. Could be added as a new failure row F-n 'APS local line swept'.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.2: balancing list includes 'capital moved to operations' (l.146, BB27 p.2-3); diversion up to $40M, cut to $20M (l.154, l.157, l.163, CIPpol p.6/p.18/p.21); capital revenue $246M short (l.148); SG142/SG143 rows are all 'EST' (l.140, CIP27m l.292-294, l.1218-1224). Not in 02: F-k/q_dir is a static draw with no link to time or HSIP state (D3.5, D10). No document shows an APS line being swept.

kept.behaviour: Finance veto or decoupling of the SG015 carrier bundle: the budget manager keeps SG015 as a stand-alone HSIP application, or takes APS back out of it, to protect SG015's BCR margin, its share of the $10M cap and its schedule from partner, PIF and 5-year-clock risk. This happens even when the mechanical package BCR is at or above 5.0, so PW1 fails by choice rather than through F-a.
kept.parameter: p_bundle_veto (probability, once per window before or after packing, that finance withholds the APS-carrying instance even though it passes BCR >= 5.0); optional margin threshold delta_margin
kept.range: p_bundle_veto U(0, 0.6); optional delta_margin U(0, 2.0) BCR points; 0 reproduces the current model
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 packing algorithm (finance gate after step 4 and before SUBMIT), D3.6 PW1 start condition; interacts with F-g
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: SG015 ($1.1M) and SG142 ($488,144) are separate rows in the same CIP, same FY28 column, same 'HSIP Cycle13 - EST' source (l.442); the SG015 corridors hold only about 1 unfunded C intersection (l.444); SG142 schedule risk, with a 2027-07 start against 2027-03/04 approval and 15-28 months to CON (l.420-421); decision rule 'protect SGR, fund by stage (readiness)' (l.154). Not in 02: D3.3 packing stops only on a mechanical BCR, and PW1 forces the bundle. No document shows a finance veto.

kept.behaviour: Soft match and labour recoding: finance covers the 10% local match of an APS-carrying package with Signal Shop staff hours, or by recoding existing work orders as capital, instead of with new cash. The cost moves out of the cash budget and into crew workload.
kept.parameter: softmatch_share (share of the 10% local match covered by in-kind Signal Shop hours or recoded labour)
kept.range: U(0, 1) (one run proposed 0-0.5 for the recoding variant); 0 = all-cash match (current model). Each unit adds crew-months to strain(t) and lowers K_crew after award.
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 local match and 'added budget' accounting (cost_by_actor), D3.2 strain(t), D3.4 internal queue K_crew
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: 'staff hours may count as soft match' (§2.4 l.203, QA13 Q14/Q59; §5 l.604); 2025-02 budget options 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital' and move 25% of paint/sign shop staff to capital (§2.2 l.158, staffing p.9/p.17; Signal Shop not named); CIP proposes to 'expand the definition of capital investment' (l.159, CIPpol p.10); 8 of 21 signal electrician positions already sit on the project-support fund recovered from capital (l.104). The rule is documented; its use for APS specifically is an inference. 02 treats the match only as a 10% cash share (D3.3).

kept.behaviour: Hold local money while HSIP is pending: finance does not commit local flexible money to APS scope that is in a pending or awarded HSIP application, to avoid double funding or supplanting, and releases it only after a rejection. This adds a lag between the failure signal and the local fallback, and after an award it removes local top-up money for the same scope.
kept.parameter: t_hold (months between the HSIP failure signal and release of local APS money), switch sw_escrow
kept.range: t_hold U(0, 12) months; sw_escrow in {0, 1}; sw_escrow = 0 reproduces the current model
kept.rule_modified: D3.6 PW1 signpost-to-local step and D3.5 F-k: the local-money event is scheduled at signal + t_hold, then the next §O3 local window (Jan-Jun preparation, Jul decision) applies. Partly overlaps that window timing already.
kept.evidence: No document in 01 supports the hold itself. Context verified: 'most flexible money goes to match' (l.149, CIPpol p.11); 'fund urgent needs by stage' (l.154). 02 has no post-signal hold; F-j t_defer applies only to the Prop L amendment.

dropped.behaviour: Hold-and-defer at the window edge or deliberate window-skipping: a finance gate before PREPARING (run 1 p_gate, run 4 p_defer_window)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.1. A multiplier on p_start is absorbed by β0's wide prior U(-6.9, -2.9) and by m_C·costpress(t) (D3.2/D10). A deliberate skip and a MISSED window produce the same state transition (IDLE, then the next window, per D3.1 and D3.6). The model has no observable that tells them apart.

dropped.behaviour: Budget-line relabel or merge of SG142 into SG015 (run 1 sw_line_merge, run 2 sw_host_relabel)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.6 PW1 (APS bundled with SG015) and D3.3 (BCR on full cost, APS reported as 'added budget'). Eligibility is judged on application content, so a plan-row label has no causal hook. Run 2's variant, which builds the bundle outside p_start, contradicts D3.1 as the sole behaviour layer. No document shows a relabel.

dropped.behaviour: Stale funded-looking placeholder row after a lost award (run 1 p_stale)
dropped.reason: Cannot act on the model. D3.6 signposts read C13 approved lists, not plan rows, and advocate pressure is exogenous (λ_press, k, F-m in D10). The proposal is also several linked parameters and does not reduce to one switch. 01 l.624 shows near-zero advocate activity. No document support.

dropped.behaviour: Reserve-for-match priority: SG000 or the director 10% earmarked as match for other federal bids (run 2 m_match_claim)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.5 F-k / D10 q_dir U(0, 0.8). An exogenous 'share of the pool claimed by others' is the same quantity as a flat probability that the pool is not used for APS, because the other bids are not modelled. The endogenous parts are kept in the sweep and hold items.

dropped.behaviour: Internal rationing of the $10M agency cap across SF's own HSIP bids (run 3 cap_reserve_other)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.3 and D10 R_other U(0, 10M), the share of the cap used by SF's other HSIP applications. cap_reserve_other only reshapes that same range. Its match_release_budget part duplicates F-k.

dropped.behaviour: Reimbursement cash-flow gating of front money and match release (run 4 t_fin_hold, p_hold)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.4. t_con is an empirical lognormal fitted to SF's observed award-to-CON times of 15-28 months (D10 t_con_med), so it already includes any historical finance release delay. Adding it again double-counts. No document support.

kept.behaviour: Discretionary and local flexible money is used up by the operating deficit (and by match for larger grants) before APS is considered. The 10% director adjustment, SG000 and the small general-fund APS row are the same flexible cash that the capital-to-operating transfer draws on, so in a deficit year little or nothing is left for an APS batch. Finance never says no to APS; the money is gone first.
kept.parameter: k_deficit: how strongly the operating gap cuts the money APS can use. q_dir_eff(t) = q_dir × (1 − k_deficit × deficit_share(t)) and A_local(t) = A_local0 × (1 − k_deficit × deficit_share(t)), where deficit_share = the operating gap divided by its FY27 level ($307M → $434M series); k_deficit = 0 gives the current static model
kept.range: U(0, 1), inferred; 0 in the control run
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-k and D10 q_dir (l.382, now constant U(0, 0.8)) plus D10 A_local (l.358, now static U(0, 0.57M)); this also weakens the end step of PW1 (l.241). 02 has no capital-to-operating transfer rule.
kept.evidence: Every input checked in 01 §2.2: l.145 operating gap $307M/$344M/$434M; l.146 'capital moved to operations' is on the balancing list; l.149 'the most flexible money goes to match'; l.154 CIP rule allows up to $40M operating diversion; l.156 director may adjust up to 10% (~$65M); l.157 board wants diversions 'one-time', cut to $20M, spread so no project loses all funding; l.163 $20–40M per round; l.139 SG000 $1.6M + $0.5M; l.162 local APS money $0–0.57M. No document shows any of this money being taken away from APS. That link is inference.

kept.behaviour: Finance books Signal Shop install labour, or reorganised work orders, to capital (the 'widen the capital definition' option). In-house APS installs on C-type intersections then draw on an existing capital line instead of new local cash. 'No money' stays true for cash, but not for labour.
kept.parameter: p_capitalize: yearly probability that finance starts booking C-type APS install labour to capital. Once on, it adds a funding pool b_cap per year to the internal route (Fi → I).
kept.range: p_capitalize U(0, 0.5) per year; b_cap U(0, 250k) per year; both inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.4 internal route (Fi → I, l.205) funding condition and D10 A_local. This differs from PW5 b_hw (l.246, a design rule on hardware replacements that advocates demand) and PW6 SG017 (l.245, scope in an existing line): here finance decides, and the rule applies whatever pathway is chosen.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.2: l.158 2025-02 budget options 'move 25% of paint and sign shop staff to capital priorities' and 'restructure work orders so they count as capital projects' ($2.5M), with a note that Signal Shop is not named; l.159 FY27-31 CIP proposes to widen the capital-investment definition to maintenance that extends life 5+ years; l.153 signals are among the most degraded assets and SGR money is 'extremely limited'. 01 l.113 (grants that pay Signal Shop labour ease the operating deficit) is itself marked 【推断】. No source applies this to APS.

kept.behaviour: Readiness-only funding. When pressed, finance pays only for scoping, design or BCR work on a few intersections and holds construction until an outside grant (HSIP) is won. This is cited to the CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise readiness)'. It looks like a response and soaks up pressure, but it produces no installs. Run 1's version is the gate form of the same rule: no local construction money until a design or grant exists.
kept.parameter: p_ready: probability that a pressure event is answered with design-only funding. When it fires: D_prep for the next window is cut, part of pressure(t) is removed, and no construction batch is created.
kept.range: p_ready U(0, 0.4), inferred; D_prep cut 1–3 months; share of pressure removed U(0.3, 0.8)
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 pressure-event branch (l.124–125, now only p_deflect and 1 − p_deflect) gets a third branch; it also changes D_prep (l.344). 02 D3.4 (l.205) designs only after the local batch is funded, and sw_pe (l.367) covers HSIP design only, so a local design-only grant is not in the model.
kept.evidence: 01 §2.2 l.154 checked: the CIP draft rule includes 「按阶段资助紧急需要（提高项目/补助就绪度）」 (fund urgent needs in phases, raise project/grant readiness), CIPpol p.6. That the rule is used on APS, or as a way to stall, has no source.

kept.behaviour: Placeholder rows. Finance points to an APS row in the CIP marked as funded by a future grant ('EST'). No application and no local backfill stand behind the row. It eases advocate pressure for a while, then lapses or rolls over at the next CIP or HSIP cycle.
kept.parameter: p_placeholder: probability that a pressure event with no active application is answered with a placeholder row. While the row is live, pressure(t) is multiplied by d_row, and the row lapses at the next HSIP/CIP window with no backfill.
kept.range: p_placeholder U(0, 0.6); d_row U(0.3, 0.8); row lifetime set by the next window (12–30 months); all inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 pressure-event branch (l.124–125) gets a third outcome, 'absorbed by placeholder'. 02 now uses the EST label only in the BCR denominator (D3.3 l.191).
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.140 SG142 (HSIP C13 – EST) and SG143 (HSIP C14 – EST + $570k general fund – EST); l.224 FY25-29 CIP planned SG136 'APS FY25' $1.0M from HSIP Cycle 12, but the full C12 list of 330 applications has no SF APS application (【事实】); l.109 SG136 has no funding row in FY27-31 (inference, strong). So a funded-looking row with no application behind it is documented. Using such a row to answer pressure, and its effect on pressure, has no source.

kept.behaviour: Local-match triage. Finance will not commit the 10% local match for an APS-bearing HSIP or SS4A package, because the flexible match money is already promised to larger grants. Without that commitment the package is held or not started. Staff-hour soft match can loosen this gate.
kept.parameter: q_match: probability that a ready grant package is deferred one cycle because no match is committed; switch match_soft (staff-hour soft match allowed) halves q_match
kept.range: q_match U(0, 0.5), inferred; match_soft ∈ {0, 1}
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 SUBMIT transition and D3.3 Route A, before the BCR ≥ 5.0 test; it adds a failure type to the D3.5 F-series. 02 now treats the 10% match only as a cost line (l.190); F-a to F-m have no match gate.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.203 HSIP reimburses 90%, local match 10%, staff hours can count as soft match (QA13 Q14, Q59); l.149 the most flexible money must go to match; l.148 capital revenue ~$246M below the last CIP, 'not enough to fund all approved projects'; l.240 Tenderloin match: $5.6M federal + $1.4M Prop L (20%); l.237 SG106/SG115 commitments. No source says APS was denied match.

dropped.behaviour: Wait-for-window deferral (run 3): r tied to the budget calendar, with repeated re-deferral
dropped.reason: Already covered. In 02 D3.1 (l.121) a task leaves IDLE only when the window opens and U < p_start, and the local window is tied to the budget calendar (Jan–Jun, decision Jul 1; l.82). After DEFLECTED a restart is therefore already calendar-gated, and repeated rolling is already the effect of a low p_start at each window.

dropped.behaviour: Cost overstatement in the deflection reply (run 1): cost_overstate, the ratio of stated to real unit cost
dropped.reason: One run only, and it would not fit in the top 5. The deflection itself is in D3.1 (p_deflect, l.124; l.342) and the cost range in u0 U(22k, 50k) (l.356). The citation, 01 l.637 C4, records an unresolved conflict between two estimates ($22k vs $40k), not deliberate overstatement. The credibility penalty adds a second mechanism, so it is not a single parameter.

dropped.behaviour: Readiness gate before any local money (run 1, readiness_gate + t_ready)
dropped.reason: Merged into the kept readiness-only funding item (same source, 01 l.154).

dropped.behaviour: Separate sweep/raid variants: run 1 sweep_rate, run 2 sweep_local, run 3 rho_raid pool
dropped.reason: Merged into the kept k_deficit item (4 runs).

dropped.behaviour: SGR / work-order reclassification variants: run 1 p_reclass, run 2 q_relabel
dropped.reason: Merged into the kept p_capitalize item (3 runs).

kept.behaviour: Outage-triggered raid on the restored APS line. After the EP17 amendment passes, each visible outage or controller-failure event leads finance to reprogram part of that year's dedicated APS money (and SG000 / 10% headroom) to controller replacement. The line stays on paper but pays out less.
kept.parameter: λ_outage (outage events per year) + f_raid (share of the year's remaining A_local diverted per event), as new event F-n
kept.range: λ_outage U(0.1, 0.5)/yr (2 precedents, 2022 and 2025; uncalibrated); f_raid U(0, 0.8), 0 = current model
kept.rule_modified: New F-n in D3.5 acting on A_local (D10) when dedicated_line = 1 / PW2 line; turns PW6's static q_sg017_block into an event-driven value. Not covered: q_sg017_block is a static per-grant probability for SG017 only, and no rule takes money back from a line after it opens
kept.evidence: Checked. 01 l.176: 'visible failures drive it: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7) is tagged 【推断】 (inference) in 01. l.126: $1M of EP17 hardware money went to ~98 controllers while the 2023 PIF listed APS as eligible 【事实】 (fact). l.179: ~202% over-programmed 【事实】 (fact). No document shows a dedicated line being raided after it was restored.

kept.behaviour: Sponsor-side hold. Finance (SFMTA is the only applicant) delays sending the amendment to the SFCTA board, folding it into the 2027-fall to 2028 5YPP window or waiting until controller needs are settled. This is time lost before any board veto or deferral.
kept.parameter: q_self_defer (probability SFMTA holds the request; if it fires, submission moves to the next 5YPP window, otherwise a short lag t_sponsor)
kept.range: q_self_defer U(0, 0.6); window 2027-10 to 2028-06; otherwise t_sponsor U(0, 9) months (hypothesis)
kept.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2 start: amendment time = trigger + delay, before F-j is drawn; θ_defer counts total delay. Not covered: in F-j only the SFCTA board vetoes or defers (q_veto, t_defer)

kept.range: U(0, 1); 0 = current model

kept.behaviour: Cost re-attribution of the ramp/conduit share. After design, the finance manager charges part of the ramp-and-conduit cost of an over-budget local batch to another payer (Public Works curb-ramp program, the General Fund ADA right-of-way money, or a concurrent paving/signal project already digging), so the APS batch carries a smaller gap. The overrun is moved, not paid, and the shifted work waits on the other program's schedule.
kept.parameter: f_shift (share of the ramp/conduit cost moved off the APS batch; 0 = current model) with companion lag t_shift_delay
kept.range: f_shift U(0, 0.6) (runs ranged 0–0.8 / 0.3–1.0; 0.6 is the conservative merge); t_shift_delay U(3, 18) months (inferred; 01 §2.11 l.374 ramp-designer shortage and C35/C36 6–9.5-year contract paths, l.377, say long lags are realistic but give no number for this)
kept.rule_modified: F-f gap handling (02 D3.5 l.225): add a cost-reassignment step after contingency and before q_topup / TERMINATED; shifted sites enter the D3.4 internal queue t_shift_delay months later. NB 02 fixes pipe/ramp (q_pipe, q_ramp, +$200k each) into planned cost at list-entry, so f_shift must act on that known ramp/conduit component (or the excess attributed to it), not on the lognormal σ_over noise.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: ramp payers exist — GF ADA right-of-way $55M FY26-30/$71M FY31-35 (§2.6 l.257, CP-I p.4; summary l.72 '$125M/10 yr flows to curb ramps'); mayor's budget lists priority curb ramps as citywide capital priority (§2.6 l.258); PW curb ramps FY26 $4.0M, FY27/28 requests $8.1M/$12.2M (§2.11 l.373 — run 1 mislabelled it s2.10, run 2 §2.12); pipe ~$200k, ramp ~$200k (§2.1 l.119); excavation triggers ramp work (l.117). Reclassification language 'reorganise work orders so they count as capital' (§2.2 l.158) is real but is about Paint & Sign shop labour, not ramps. CP-T p.11 (l.265) says accessibility capital sits in other departments' budgets 'including traffic and signals (APS)' — real, but it describes where APS money sits, not ramp-cost shifting. Counter-signal: DPW says ramp construction does not trigger APS and APS 'is MTA's matter' (§2.11 l.376). No document shows any APS cost being shifted.

kept.behaviour: Triage/descoping within the batch with refill. Instead of terminating the over-budget project or site, the manager keeps the batch money fixed, drops the highest-cost (conduit/ramp-heavy) sites back to the pool, and uses the freed money to fund the cheapest pending C-type sites. More installs come early; the expensive tail becomes the persistent never_served set.
kept.parameter: sw_triage (0 = current F-f TERMINATED branch; 1 = drop highest-realized-cost sites until the batch fits plan×(1+κ_cont), then refill from cheapest pool C-type sites at u0)
kept.range: {0, 1}; a ranking switch (cost_desc vs random) can be a scenario variant, not a separate swept parameter
kept.rule_modified: F-f (02 l.225) and the D3.4 TERMINATED paragraph (l.209): replace 'project/site TERMINATED, back to pool' with cost-ranked drop + refill. 02 already allows the overrun site alone to be TERMINATED and returned to the pool (l.225 '项目 / 该路口 TERMINATED'), so the new parts are only the cost ranking and the refill.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: remaining sites 'selected based on funding' (§2.1 l.130, MDC26 p.8); unit cost $40k–$1.5M and 'easy intersections already done, harder and costlier' (§2.1 l.118–119); SG142 is a ~22-site no-excavation, all-Signal-Shop batch (§2.2 l.139), i.e. no-dig subsets are already used as units; CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise readiness)' (§2.2 l.155, CIPpol p.6) and board 'spread so no project loses funding' (l.157, CIPpol p.18/p.21) are real but are about capital-to-operations diversions/phasing, not mid-batch descoping. No document of descoping an APS batch.

kept.behaviour: Shared, depleting discretionary pool. The cumulative 10% director adjustment (and SG000 reserve) is drawn on by all SFMTA capital overruns and capital-to-operations moves, so the chance that an APS overrun is covered falls as other claims use up the room, and recovers when the budget resets. Correlates failures in bad years.
kept.parameter: u_other (share of the year's discretionary room already used by other claims when the APS request arrives); q_dir_t = q_dir × (1 − u_other), same scaling applied to q_topup
kept.range: u_other U(0.3, 1.0) (inferred); u_other = 0 recovers current model; reset each biennial budget
kept.rule_modified: F-k q_dir (02 l.230, static U(0, 0.8)) and the F-f q_topup draw (l.225, static U(0, 0.7)): replace fixed probabilities with pool-scaled ones; PW1/PW2 last step 'director 10% / general fund' (l.241) inherits it.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.2: director may adjust capital budget within cumulative ≤10% (≈$65M, amount inferred) without the board (l.156, RES l.22/l.82); SG000 $1.6M FY27 + $0.5M FY28 (l.137); operating gap $307M FY27 (l.143) and balancing list includes moving capital to operations (l.144); board wants diversions one-time, cut $40M→$20M (l.157). Run 3's '10% per year' is wrong — 01 says cumulative. Competing claimants and how APS ranks among them have no document; whether the 10%/SG000 can be used for APS at all is itself marked 待核 in 02 l.382. Run 3's pool_cap U($0.5M,$6M) and run 2's B_disc up to $65M disagree by an order of magnitude — collapsed to a share-used parameter to avoid inventing a dollar size.

kept.behaviour: Hold the top-up request for a later budget window. At design-complete the manager neither approves nor refuses the over-contingency gap but parks it until the next budget decision; the designed sites sit idle (out of the Signal Shop queue) and cost may drift up meanwhile.
kept.parameter: p_hold (share of over-contingency gaps parked instead of decided at once); wait length is not a new parameter — the request resolves at the next local-field decision date already in 02 (July 1), q_topup re-drawn on cost inflated by existing g_cost
kept.range: p_hold U(0, 0.7) (inferred); p_hold = 0 recovers current model
kept.rule_modified: F-f (02 l.225): insert PARKED state before the q_topup draw, exiting at the next 02 §local-field decision date (l.82, July 1 annually); D3.4 internal queue entry delayed accordingly. Existing pauses don't cover it: t_pause is only for the F-e outsourcing gap (l.224), t_defer only for the Prop L vote (F-j, l.229).
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: general-fund requests are two-year, due before 5-01 in even years (§3.1 l.412); TNC is pay-as-you-go, programmed one year at a time (§2.3 l.187); board budget schedule 2025-11→2026-04, 8 sessions, no accessibility/signal item (§2.2 l.160); unit price rising ~9–10%/yr (§2.1 l.119). These show decisions happen in discrete windows; no document shows a finance manager deliberately parking an APS overrun.

dropped.behaviour: Run 3 logit for q_topup/q_dir with w_press × pressure(t) and readiness term; run 2 deficit_share scaling of q_topup
dropped.reason: Multi-coefficient functional form, not one parameter or switch; folded into the single u_other scaling of the kept pool item. Readiness preference is not documented for overrun cover (CIPpol p.6 'phase to raise readiness' is about phasing funding, not ranking overruns).

dropped.behaviour: Run 2 q_expire: waiting breaks the 1.5-year install clock or a match deadline

Also 01 l.68 and 02 say the clock has no penalty in practice.

dropped.behaviour: Separate dollar-sized pool parameters (B_disc U($2M,$65M), pool_cap U($0.5M,$6M), B_dir U($5M,$65M)) and claim-arrival rates lambda_claim
dropped.reason: Duplicates of the pool item; dollar size of the discretionary room usable for overruns is not in 01 (the $65M is an inferred 10% of the whole capital budget, l.156), so a dollar range would invent a fact. Kept as a single share-used parameter.
