kept.behaviour: Discretion and flexible local money released only as HSIP match: the director's 10% and SG000 are held back and used for the 10% local match and the ineligible costs of an approved HSIP package, not as stand-alone APS money. While a C13/C14 bid is pending, local APS money (including any APS slice of SG017) waits for the result. If HSIP fails, the money is released late or goes to other needs. This links the HSIP and local channels, which 02 currently draws independently. (Merges run1 match-first, run2 SG017 hold, run3 bridge/payback, run4 contingent match.)
kept.parameter: sw_dir_match (0/1) with q_dir_match
kept.range: sw_dir_match in {0,1}; when 1: stand-alone q_dir = 0, q_dir_match U(0.3, 0.95) applied at the HSIP award event; if no award, fallback q_dir_eff = q_dir·(1 − q_dir_match) and release lag t_hold U(0, 9) months
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-k (q_dir U(0,0.8), l.230), the PW1 last-resort node (D3.6 l.241), and the HSIP 10% local match (D3.3/D10). It replaces the independent q_dir draw with a draw conditional on HSIP state
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.149 (§2.2, CIPpol p.11) 'the most flexible money has to go to match' [fact]; l.68 the same rule in the summary table; l.156 the director can adjust up to 10% cumulatively without the Board (RES l.22, l.82) [fact; the $65M figure is calculated]; l.203 HSIP reimburses 90%, local match 10% (QA13 Q14, Q59). The match rule is documented. Holding money until the award and releasing it on the award is inferred: no document describes it.

kept.behaviour: Readiness tranche: instead of buying APS hardware, finance releases a small staged amount for a pole and conduit survey, design and PIF work on C-class intersections. This applies the CIP rule 'fund urgent needs in phases to raise project/grant readiness'. It installs nothing. It shortens preparation for the next HSIP window or SG017 call and settles whether the 'conduits and poles satisfactory' condition holds.
kept.parameter: g_ready (share of the a_sg017 / discretion pool spent on readiness), with sw_readiness
kept.range: g_ready U(0, 0.4) (or a_ready U($0, $100k)/FY); effect on surveyed C-class intersections: D_prep and t_des multiplied by (1 − U(0.2, 0.5)), and up to +0.2 on the share confirmed poles-OK
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 PREPARING duration (D_prep U(1,6), l.137/l.344, now static), t_des in D3.4, and the PW6 eligibility pool (D3.6 l.245); it also takes part of a_sg017 (D10 l.375)
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 l.154 (§2.2, CIPpol p.6): the draft CIP rule is 'fund urgent needs in phases (raise project/grant readiness)' [fact]. 01 l.446: the SG017 CIP scope allows new APS only 'where it is determined that the existing conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition' [fact]. The rule is documented, but no document shows SFMTA paying for an APS pole and conduit survey.

kept.behaviour: Fault-shock reprioritisation: a visible signal failure (a blackout or a controller firewall finding) pulls unspent SG017 money back to controllers and cabinets in that year. So the SG017 block is driven by events and clusters in time; it is not a fixed draw each cycle.
kept.parameter: lambda_fault (annual failure-shock rate), with kappa_block (jump in q_sg017_block that decays over t_fault)
kept.range: lambda_fault U(0.2, 1.0)/yr; kappa_block U(0.1, 0.5), q_block(t) = min(0.95, q_sg017_block + kappa_block·shock(t)); t_fault U(6, 24) months
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.6 PW6 signpost (l.245) and D10 q_sg017_block (U(0.2,0.9), l.375). F-a to F-m contain no controller-failure event
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.126 says EP17 hardware money of $1M (FY25+26) went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects (OCT25 p.7) [fact]. l.447 says FY24 went to cabinets, detectors and RRFB, and FY25-26 to controllers, and FY27-28 use is unknown [fact]. The causal link, l.176 'outcomes are visible-failure driven: controllers got EP17 money after the 2022 and 2025 blackouts', is tagged 【推断】 in 01 and sits in §2.3 (SFCTA), not in the finance section.

kept.behaviour: One-off cap on discretion: a director-discretion or SG000 draw for APS is treated as a one-off. After it has been used for APS it is not available again for several years, so an early local APS batch removes the later fallback.
kept.parameter: n_dir_max (maximum discretion draws for APS over the horizon)
kept.range: n_dir_max in {0, 1, 2} over 5 years (run3 offered {1,2,3}); after the cap is reached q_dir = 0
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-k and D10 q_dir (l.382). The draw is no longer repeated independently each time
kept.evidence: 01 l.157 (CIPpol p.18, p.21) verified: the Board wants diversions to be 'one-time' and 'spread out so no project loses funding'. That text is about capital-to-operating diversions ($40M to $20M), not the director's 10% adjustment (l.156). Applying it to APS discretion is an extrapolation. Run2's other proposal, making q_dir depend on the deficit, is folded in here and not kept: the deficit path in 01 l.145 ($307M to $344M to $434M) is high every year, so it adds almost no variation.

dropped.behaviour: Pre-emptive controller carve-out s_ctrl_pre (run1)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D10 a_sg017 U(0, 250k), capped at half of SG017 (02 l.375). (1 − s_ctrl_pre)·500k with s_ctrl_pre in U(0.5, 1) gives the same range. It changes who is said to cause the split, not how the model behaves.

dropped.behaviour: Scope-wording hedge p_scope_hedge: APS eligible but no earmark (run3)
dropped.reason: Already covered by q_sg017_block U(0.2, 0.9) and a_sg017 (D3.6 PW6 l.245, D10 l.375). An extra independent probability that sets a_sg017 = 0 is the same as a higher block probability.

dropped.behaviour: Request-language laundering / side deal with Signal Shop (run1)
dropped.reason: Mostly a duplicate of the scope hedge, so q_sg017_block and a_sg017 cover it. The side deal has no document support. The proposal needs three pieces (a switch, a release probability and a factor on scope rejection), so it is not one parameter. 01 l.446 is cited correctly, but it only shows the conditional wording in the CIP scope.

dropped.behaviour: Token APS batch with pressure relief (n_token, r_press_relief, t_relief) (run1)
dropped.reason: Needs three parameters. The pressure-relief effect has no document. 01 l.155 and l.140 are real but do not support it. Batch size is already set by the local margin in D3.1, and pressure decay by k and F-m.

dropped.behaviour: Year-phasing and ratchet (phi_aps_year, rho_ratchet) (run4)
dropped.reason: Two parameters with no document. a_sg017 is already drawn per year (D10). The citation 01 l.204 for the Board wanting spreading is wrong: l.204 is a Caltrans row, and the Board text is at l.157.

dropped.behaviour: Labor capitalisation f_cap (run2)
dropped.reason: Its only effect in the model is a lower effective u0 (at most about 35%), which the sampled u0 U(22k, 50k) range already covers (D10 l.356). The 2025 options are real (01 l.158, l.159), but Signal Shop is not named and the effect on audit risk is outside the model.

dropped.behaviour: Deficit-dependent q_dir_t = clip(q_dir0 + a·deficit + b·failure) (run2)
dropped.reason: Split up. The failure link is merged into the fault-shock item and the cumulative cap into the one-off cap item. The deficit term adds almost no variation because 01 l.145 shows the deficit high in every year.

kept.behaviour: Staff hold before the board: SFCTA programming staff do not put a Prop L EP17 APS amendment (PW2) on the board agenda while an HSIP C13 application for APS is pending (results about 2027-03/04). They may also advise folding the request into the next Strategic Plan / 5YPP cycle (starts autumn 2027, adopted 2028). This is a staff-stage delay with no vote. Merged from run 1 sw_wait_hsip, run 2 q_hold and run 4 q_fold.
kept.parameter: q_hold (probability that staff hold a PW2/PW6 amendment while an APS-bearing HSIP instance is pending or a 5YPP update is near). The delay is a derived quantity: months until the C13 result, or until the next 5YPP window in the fold-in branch. It is not a free parameter.
kept.range: q_hold U(0, 0.7), inferred. 0 reproduces the current model. Run 4 proposes scaling it by (1 - pressure_visible).
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (the proposals wrongly cite D3.2; F-j sits in D3.5) and the D3.6 PW2 start rule. It adds a staff pre-gate before the board branch. Today F-j acts only after a board veto or deferral, and only then does it mention waiting for the next 5YPP.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. l.185: staff evaluate, then CAC, then board (SP p.22) [fact]. l.179: EP17 5YPP $27.49M committed against $8.52M pay-go, about 202% ahead, no APS row [fact]. l.180: 'next five years not expected to be this far ahead' [fact]. l.192: next 5YPP starts autumn 2027 and is adopted 2028 [fact]. l.411: a revision can happen at any time, precedent 3-4 months. l.421: C13 approval 2027-03/04 (a 01 inference line). No source shows staff holding or redirecting an amendment. Overlap note: F-j t_defer U(1,12) already covers the size of the delay. The only new part is that the hold depends on whether an HSIP application is pending.

kept.behaviour: Zero-sum offset / visibility-row swap: EP17 is over-programmed, so staff will only add an APS row if an existing EP17 row gives up money. The candidate is the Prop L visibility row ($0.4M/yr). Staff move part of it to APS, most plausibly once SG015 visibility goes into or wins HSIP C13. Merged from run 2 q_swap, run 3 f_swap and run 4 p_offset_required. Run 1 PW6b, which uses the same visibility row as a scope-stretch, was folded in here so the same $0.4M/yr is not counted twice.
kept.parameter: f_swap (share of the $0.4M/yr EP17 visibility row moved to APS and added to A_local). Optional switch sw_swap conditions it on SG015 being in an HSIP package or award.
kept.range: f_swap U(0, 0.5), inferred. 0 is the control and reproduces the baseline.
kept.rule_modified: D10 A_local (the local-field allocation for APS) and the D3.6 PW2 / PW6 start conditions. It couples PW2 to the D3.3 SG015 outcome.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. l.179: the EP17 FY26-28 visibility row is $0.4M/yr and there is no APS row [fact]. l.411: uncommitted headroom is $0-0.5M/yr. l.239: SG015 is funded by HSIP C13 $1.1M (FY28) plus SS4A $2.4M, both EST, and Prop L is not listed. l.442: SG015 and SG142 sit side by side with the same C13 source [fact]. Caveat: 01 never links the Prop L visibility row to SG015. Per l.239, SG015 is not a Prop L line, so the premise that HSIP 'frees' Prop L money is unverified. 02 has no offset or swap rule: F-j is veto/defer only, PW6 is SG017 only, and F-k is director reserve only.

kept.behaviour: NTP side route: a district supervisor, possibly pointed there by SFCTA staff, uses the Neighbourhood Transportation Program (EP25, $700k per district over 5 years) to fund APS design at specific intersections. This follows the D4 Lincoln Way precedent, needs no SFMTA-initiated EP17 amendment, and bypasses the A2 task. It funds design, not construction.
kept.parameter: p_ntp_use (annual probability, per district, that NTP is used for APS design). It runs as a new pathway branch PW7 under switch sw_ntp. The amount is capped by the documented $700k per district per 5 years.
kept.range: p_ntp_use U(0, 0.3) per district-year, inferred. The amount cap of $700k per district per 5 years is fixed from the evidence. The lead time uses the 3-4 month precedent.
kept.rule_modified: D3.6 (new PW7 branch, triggered after a PW1 failure or a DEFLECTED state) and D3.4 (it shortens t_des for the covered intersections and leaves construction funding to the existing sources). It also adds a D10 row.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. l.171: EP25 NTP, district-recommended projects, $700k per district for FY24-28 (NTP5 p.7-8) [fact]. l.177: the D4 supervisor used NTP $500k to design two new signals that included APS at Lincoln Way, and the 5YPP revision took 3-4 months (LW p.15-18) [fact]. l.269: supervisors move money through NTP recommendations [fact]. Confirmed absent from 02: a grep for NTP finds nothing, and the pathways are PW0-PW6 only. Caveat: the precedent shows a supervisor acting, not SFCTA staff steering. Run 3 cites l.170, which is EP18 with SFCTA as an applicant; that is a different program from NTP.

kept.behaviour: Local-match commitment timing: staff will not name or pre-program the 10% Prop L / local match for an APS-bearing HSIP package until the award is known. The CON step then waits for an allocation cycle, or for the next 5YPP window if the match must sit in an approved line first. Merged from run 1 q_match_ok, which gates before submission, and run 3 t_match_gap, which delays after award.
kept.parameter: t_match_gap (months added to the CON E-76 formula for APS-bearing HSIP projects whose match is not yet programmed). It is controlled by switch sw_match_gate, default 0.
kept.range: t_match_gap U(0, 6) months. With the 5YPP-wait variant, U(0, 18). Both inferred. Allocation lead time is 8-13 weeks (01 l.193).
kept.rule_modified: D3.4 HSIP row: CON E-76 = max(design done, PIF, cycle start + t_con), plus t_match_gap. Today D3.3 treats the 10% match as available, and the only nearby rule, q_topup in F-e/F-f, covers overruns rather than the base match.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. l.203 and l.604: HSIP reimburses 90%, with a 10% local match [fact]. l.185: allocation is based on the applicant package, and staff review it [fact]. l.193: allocation takes 8-13 weeks with no August meeting [fact]. l.240: in the Tenderloin SS4A project, Prop L $1.4M was the named match (20%) [fact], so Prop L as a match is real practice. No source shows staff withholding a match. Caveat that weakens run 1's pre-submission gate: l.203 says staff hours count as a soft match, so a missing cash match probably does not block submission. For that reason only the post-award delay form is kept.

dropped.behaviour: Run 1: Prop L bridge / cash-flow advance so that Signal Shop starts before CON E-76 (q_bridge, a_bridge, q_bridge_loss)
dropped.reason: It needs three parameters, so it cannot be written as one parameter or switch. It also contradicts D3.4, where CON E-76 and PIF are hard preconditions for internal federal-aid construction; 01 l.421 calls PIF a legal precondition (LAPM ch.12). No source supports an advance.

dropped.behaviour: Run 4: contingent pre-commitment of Prop L match or top-up, with q_topup_cond replacing q_topup
dropped.reason: Covered by D10 / D3.5 F-e and F-f. q_topup U(0, 0.7) already spans the proposed range, so the proposal is a re-range, not a new rule. It also mixes the base 10% match with overrun top-ups; the match-timing part is merged into the kept match-timing item.

dropped.behaviour: Run 2: staff steer SFMTA before the deadline to bundle APS with SG015 instead of the APS-only SG142 (p_steer)
dropped.reason: Covered by D3.6 PW1, which is already the bundling arm, and by the D3.3 packaging algorithm, which only forms instances with a carrier and BCR ≥ 5.0. A nudge toward PW1 is what the PW1 vs PW0 comparison already measures. No source gives SFCTA a role in HSIP (a Caltrans program).

dropped.behaviour: Run 3: staff triage before the deadline that keeps the APS-only line out (q_prescreen)
dropped.reason: Covered by D3.3 packaging steps ①-④ and F-a: an APS-only line with no carrier or BCR < 5.0 never becomes a submitted instance. Run 3 itself notes that the SFCTA pre-screening role is unverified.

dropped.behaviour: Run 1: APS as a scope add-on inside the Prop L visibility row, without an amendment (a_vis, q_vis_block, PW6b)
dropped.reason: Duplicate. It draws on the same $0.4M/yr visibility row as the kept swap item, and keeping both would count that money twice. It also needs two parameters (a_vis and q_vis_block). The scope-stretch pattern itself already exists in PW6 / q_sg017_block. 01 has no 5YPP description showing that the visibility row could carry APS.

kept.behaviour: Staff pre-filing screen: before an EP17 amendment (or an APS-bearing allocation) is filed, staff tell SFMTA informally to hold it for the 2027-28 5YPP window or that it is not ready. Nothing is submitted, so no veto is ever recorded. A board-member sponsor (Lincoln Way pattern) bypasses the screen.
kept.parameter: q_screen: probability per attempted PW2/PW6 amendment that staff redirect it to the next window (the task goes PREPARING -> IDLE, or is delayed to the window, with no REJECTED event). Optional sub-switch sw_sponsor_bypass: if a sponsor is drawn (p_sponsor), the screen is skipped.
kept.range: q_screen U(0, 0.6), 0 as control; p_sponsor U(0, 0.5)/yr; screen applies only while months to the next window < theta_window U(12, 30)
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 PREPARING->SUBMITTED transition (adds a step before F-j); D3.6 PW2 opener and the PW6 fallback. F-j (02 l.229) has only a board veto/deferral after filing, and its 'wait for the next 5YPP' is a recovery step, not a screen before filing.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.3: next strategic plan + 5YPP starts autumn 2027 and is adopted 2028 (l.193, SP p.8/10/46); amendments can happen at any time, and the D4 supervisor did one in 3-4 months with NTP $500k (l.177, LW p.15-18); allocation is 'based on a package prepared and submitted by an eligible sponsor', with staff -> CAC -> board (l.185, SP p.22). No document shows staff telling anyone not to file.

kept.behaviour: Offset or partial approval: staff recommend an APS amendment only if SFMTA names an EP17 line to cut (TSP, hardware replacement, visibility, pipeline). Otherwise staff approve only part of the request. The amendment becomes zero-sum inside EP17 rather than all-or-nothing.
kept.parameter: f_offset: share of the requested APS amount actually programmed when an offset is required. A_local_effective = min(request, headroom + f_offset x donor line). Turned on by the switch offset_required.
kept.range: offset_required in {0,1}; f_offset U(0.3, 1.0); optional t_offset U(1, 6) months for SFMTA to name the donor line
kept.rule_modified: 02 F-j (adds a partial outcome to approve/veto/defer); D10 A_local (l.358, currently U(0.5M, 2M) x APS share when dedicated_line=1, with no cap from donor lines); the Prop L steps of PW2 and PW6. Only the HSIP marginal application has partial funding (l.195).
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 l.179: the EP17 2023 5YPP commits $27.49M against $8.52M pay-go, about 202% ahead; FY26-28 is about $2.80M/yr, all of it on TSP, pipes, signs, hardware ($0.5M/yr) and visibility ($0.4M/yr); there is no APS row (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14). l.180: 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of front-loading'. So a new line needs money from an existing one, but no document shows staff demanding an offset.

kept.behaviour: Two-stage allocation with a commitment clock: staff fund design first. Construction money needs 95% plans, environmental clearance and permits, and must be committed within 12 months. A 'funded' local batch therefore needs a second approval and can lapse.
kept.parameter: Switch two_stage. When it is on, a second construction-allocation draw q_stage2 follows t_des, and if design runs past t_commit the batch lapses with probability q_lapse and goes back to IDLE.
kept.range: two_stage in {0,1}; q_stage2 U(0.6, 0.98); t_commit 12 months (sensitivity 12-18); q_lapse U(0.3, 1.0); stage-2 lead time 8-13 weeks
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.4 internal-delivery row (l.205: funded batch -> designing -> t_des -> F-f) and F-f (l.225). Adds a gate before the Fi->I queue. Neither has a second approval or a lapse deadline.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 l.182: 'construction allocation needs 95% plans, environmental clearance and permits; must be committed within 12 months of allocation' (SP p.19-23). l.195: allocation lead time is about 8-10 weeks, no August meeting, 8-13 weeks (allocation request calendar 2025/2026 p.1). Signal Shop staffing is 'often the limiting factor' (l.181, EP17-5YPP l.354-356). The q values are inferred.

kept.behaviour: Cash-flow back-loading: because EP17 is programmed about 202% ahead of pay-go, staff approve an APS allocation in principle but schedule the cash in later fiscal years. The money is approved but cannot be used yet.
kept.parameter: t_cf: months between Prop L approval and money usable for design, applied with probability q_cf_defer.
kept.range: q_cf_defer U(0, 0.6), 0 as control; t_cf U(6, 36) months
kept.rule_modified: Adds a delay between the APPROVED event and 'batch funded -> designing' in 02 D3.4 (Prop L routes only: PW2 and PW6). This is new failure path F-n. F-j t_defer (l.229) is a deferral of the vote, not a delay of cash after approval.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 l.179-180 (202% front-loading; 'the next five years are not expected to see this degree of front-loading') and l.197 (FY28/29+ pay-go about $2.0-2.8M/yr, marked as inference in 01). No document shows staff deferring the cash for an APS allocation.

kept.behaviour: Steering to a neighbouring Prop L or TNC channel: when SFMTA says 'no money', staff (or a supervisor's office) send a visible cluster to a district NTP grant, an EP18 corridor project, or the SFCTA half of the TNC tax. The request is reframed as a district safety project.
kept.parameter: Switch steer_route. Each pressure event succeeds with probability q_steer, funding n_steer intersections with a_steer dollars after a delay of t_steer. Successes join the same approval and delivery queue as a local batch.
kept.range: steer_route in {0,1}; q_steer U(0, 0.3) per pressure event; a_steer U($0.2M, $0.7M); n_steer U(2, 12); t_steer U(3, 8) months
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (adds a 'steered' exit) and the D3.3 funding fields; an optional PW4 branch in D3.6. 02 has no TNC, NTP or EP18 route (grep finds none), and its only buck-passing is SFMTA's p_deflect.
kept.evidence: The channel is verified in 01: the D4 supervisor used NTP $500k to design two new signals with APS on Lincoln Way, with a 5YPP revision done in 3-4 months (l.177, LW p.15-18); NTP is $700k per district over FY24-28 (l.171, NTP5 p.7-8); the SFCTA TNC half is 'dedicated' to right-of-way safety and lists signal improvements (l.178, PROPD p.7-9), with $0 programmed to signals or APS so far (l.173, TNCm). That staff start the steering is not documented. Only the route and its timing are.

dropped.behaviour: Funder-side APS-inclusion condition on EP17/EP18 signal allocations (run2 #3, run3 #2)
dropped.reason: Cut by the 5-item cap. It is also the weakest fit: 01 l.185 records that SFCTA only allocates on packages the sponsor submits, and l.189 that no CAC memo asked about APS. Its narrowing direction is already covered by the PW6 'scope limited to replace' branch and q_sg017_block (02 l.245, l.375). The Contract 35 / C66 / C67 citations (01 l.416, OCT25 p.3, p.26-27) are real but show SFMTA policy, not staff conditions.

dropped.behaviour: Shared-pool crowd-out of APS by top-ups and controller failures (run4 #1)
dropped.reason: Mostly covered: q_sg017_block already means SG017 money taken by controller and failure priorities (02 l.245, l.375), and F-f q_topup handles overruns (l.225). The only new part is coupling these through one depleting pool, which is a coding detail of D10, not a new staff behaviour. The priority order has no document support.

dropped.behaviour: Windfall recycling of under-budget EP17/EP18 savings to APS (run4 #4)
dropped.reason: No document support (the run says so itself). 01 l.378 gives a per-site cost range, not any evidence of savings. It would be pure inference with a tiny assumed amount (U(0, 150k)), so it adds a free parameter without any grounding.

dropped.behaviour: Staff TNC programming discretion and refer-back (run3 #3)
dropped.reason: Merged into the steering item (the TNC route). The q_refer_back part repeats SFMTA's p_deflect mechanism (02 D3.1 l.124) on the funder side, and on its own it cannot be told apart from deflection in the model's outputs.

dropped.behaviour: Sponsor-gated amendments (run3 #4) and wait-for-window advice (run1 #4)
dropped.reason: Merged into the pre-filing screen item, with the sponsor as a bypass sub-switch.

dropped.behaviour: Haircut / partial approval (run2 #2, h_prop part)
dropped.reason: Merged into the offset / partial approval item. The d_cash part of the same proposal went into the cash-flow back-loading item.

kept.behaviour: SFCTA steps in as a substitute sponsor. While the SFMTA APS owner post is empty, SFCTA staff (or a district Board member, steered by staff toward NTP) create an APS-bearing item themselves. That can be an EP18 corridor or planning item, where SFCTA is itself an eligible applicant, or a small NTP-style design amendment. The money therefore does not wait for an A2 request. NTP items produce design-only money, and delivery still depends on SFMTA (Signal Shop, F-e/F-f).
kept.parameter: p_sfcta_sponsor (switch sw_sfcta_sponsor plus a rate); a_sfcta per-instance amount
kept.range: sw_sfcta_sponsor {0,1}. p_sfcta_sponsor U(0, 0.3) per year, active only while owner = 0 (vacant) and no live instance exists for that venue; 0 reproduces the current model. a_sfcta U($0.25M, $0.5M). Optional lag t_sp U(3, 8) months. The instance still passes F-j (q_veto) and still meets K_crew / strain at delivery.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1: adds an exogenous instance-creation event that bypasses A2's IDLE→PREPARING and p_start. This partly overrides the line saying neighbouring nodes have no take-over rule. D3.6: new PW7 'SFCTA/NTP-led' path feeding the same approval step as PW2/F-j.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.3: l.170 lists EP18 applicants as 'SFMTA、SFPW、SFCTA' (EP p.12). l.171 gives NTP at $700k per district per 5 years (NTP5 p.7–8). l.177 records the D4 Board member using NTP $500k to design two APS-bearing Lincoln Way signals, with a 3–4 month 5YPP revision (LW p.15–18). l.269 (§2.12) says the mayor and the Board of Supervisors can move money indirectly through members serving as SFCTA board members and through NTP recommendations. l.185 counter-line: allocation rests on a package prepared by a qualified applicant (SP p.22). Not covered in 02: D3.1 makes A2 the only behavioural actor, and D3.6 PW2 and PW6 both start from an SFMTA request. No document shows SFCTA staff filling a vacant sponsor role on their own initiative. The precedent was driven by a Board member, not by staff.

kept.behaviour: SFCTA staff screen or return a request before the board, depending on the applicant's capacity. When the applicant has no named owner (or only a covering contact) and is under a hiring freeze, staff score the request down on readiness or return it for resubmission. Reasons include no named lead, no delivery schedule, and no confirmed Signal Shop capacity. The request is delayed or dropped before it reaches the F-j board vote. This merges run 3's readiness haircut and run 4's 'ask for resubmittal'.
kept.parameter: q_staff_return (plus vacancy multiplier m_ret)
kept.range: q_staff_return U(0, 0.4) per local-venue submission, multiplied by m_ret U(1.0, 2.0) while owner = 0 (or strain > threshold). If it fires, the request goes back to IDLE with delay d_return U(1, 4) months. 0 reproduces the current model.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 SUBMITTED → review: adds a capacity-conditional RETURNED branch before F-j. Applies to the local venue in O3, where currently a request 'goes in as a batch as soon as it is approved' against A_local. Reuses strain(t) from D3.2.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.3: l.185 says staff review comes first, then CAC, then the board (SP p.22 §2.7). l.186 shows the 5YPP score gives readiness 5 of 31 points (EP17-5YPP p.12–13). Correction: readiness is not the single highest weight, because it ties at 5 with disadvantaged communities and community support (run 2 says otherwise). l.181 quotes 'Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor' (EP17-5YPP l.354–356), and §2.1 l.90 repeats it. Not covered in 02: F-j's q_veto is an unconditional board-level draw, and the O3 local venue has no staff screen. No document shows staff returning a request on these grounds.

kept.behaviour: Staff hold a mid-cycle request until the next 5YPP. Instead of processing a standalone APS amendment or allocation, staff fold it into the 5YPP / Strategic Plan round that starts in autumn 2027. Their reasons are that EP17 is about 202% over-programmed, there is little headroom, amendments take staff time, and with the owner gone nobody is pressing for it.
kept.parameter: p_hold_to_cycle
kept.range: p_hold_to_cycle U(0, 0.6), applied when owner = 0 and months to the next 5YPP window ≤ 18–24. If it fires, the resolution date moves deterministically to the cycle date (2027-autumn to 2028), capped at 18 months, instead of the t_defer U(1, 12) draw. 0 reproduces the current model.
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D3.6 PW2/PW6: adds a staff-side hold before the board step with its own trigger (vacancy plus window proximity), separate from q_veto. D10 t_defer becomes conditional.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.3: one line commits $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go ('超前约 202%'), with FY26–28 about $2.80M per year all committed and no APS line (EP17-5YPP p.10–11, p.14). l.180 quotes 'the next five years are not expected to be this far ahead' (p.11). l.192 says the next Strategic Plan and 5YPP start in autumn 2027 and pass in 2028. l.177 shows the fast 3–4 month route happened with a Board member's push. Caveat: the FY26–28 uncommitted balance of $0–0.5M per year (l.613) is tagged 【推断】 (inference) in 01, not fact. Partly covered in 02: F-j already offers 'wait for the next 5YPP', but only after a board veto. No document shows staff choosing to hold.

kept.behaviour: Approval depends on a champion. Without the informal owner, a request that arrives with no sponsoring Board member or CAC voice gets a higher veto or deferral chance and a longer lag. A request with a champion (an NTP-style Board push) keeps the fast 3–4 month track.
kept.parameter: champion flag with q_veto_nochamp, t_defer_nochamp
kept.range: champion = owner OR pressure(t) above a threshold, or a Board-member event. q_veto_nochamp U(0.1, 0.6) versus the base q_veto U(0, 0.5). t_defer_nochamp U(3, 18) months versus U(1, 12). Turned off, it gives the current model.
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j and D10: q_veto and t_defer become conditional on the champion flag, which reuses the existing owner and pressure(t) variables.
kept.evidence: Verified: 01 §2.3 l.177 (D4 Lincoln Way, a 3–4 month 5YPP revision driven by a Board member) and l.269 (Board members move money through NTP / SFCTA board seats, NTP5 p.7–8). Not covered in 02: q_veto and t_defer are unconditional draws. Run 1's p_bundle_wait also uses 'champion = none' as its trigger. No document shows staff slow-walking requests that have no champion. The D4 case shows a champion speeding things up, not the reverse.

kept.behaviour: The thin EP17 balance erodes while nobody defends the line. With no APS request on file and no owner to defend the line, staff recommend putting the EP17 uncommitted balance toward other queued items (controller failures, TSP, hardware) in the next allocation or amendment package. By the time an APS request arrives, the slack is gone.
kept.parameter: lambda_sweep (with f_sweep)
kept.range: Monthly hazard lambda_sweep U(0, 0.04) while owner = 0. Each event removes a fraction f_sweep U(0.2, 0.6) of the remaining EP17 local headroom. 0 reproduces the current model.
kept.rule_modified: D10 A_local and a_sg017 become a depleting stock conditional on owner status, instead of a fresh per-year draw. This generalises the one-shot q_sg017_block in D3.6 PW6.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.2 l.126: the EP17 hardware $1M (FY25+FY26) went to about 98 controllers with firewall defects even though the 2023 PIF listed APS replacement as eligible (OCT25 p.7). 01 §3.2 says FY24–26 SG017 allocations show no APS use. However, the '$0–0.5M uncommitted balance' that this behaviour drains is itself tagged 【推断】 (inference) in 01 l.613. No document links any sweep to the owner vacancy. Only 1 run proposed it.

dropped.behaviour: Run 2: staff steer SFMTA to fold new APS into the SG017 hardware-replacement allocation (embedded scope)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.6 PW6 ('use the existing SG017', a_sg017, q_sg017_block). Run 2's other part, SFCTA as the EP18 applicant, was merged into kept item 1.

dropped.behaviour: Run 4: staff attach scope-narrowing conditions that thin the APS share of an approved grant (f_aps_thin)
dropped.reason: Largely covered by D10: a_sg017 U(0, 250k) already lets the APS share of SG017 run anywhere from zero up, and q_sg017_block covers 'scope limited to replace / priority faults'. The only addition, conditioning on owner_vacant, overlaps kept item 2. The source behind the scope-condition wording (CIP27m 'existing conduits and poles satisfactory', 01 §3.2) is real, but it is the CIP's own scope text, not a staff-imposed condition.

dropped.behaviour: Run 3: contact-point drift, where SFMTA budget staff or a parent-project PM inherit APS as rider scope (sw_rider_inherit)
dropped.reason: It describes an SFMTA-internal take-over, so it falls outside the SFCTA staff role being played. The vacancy itself is already F-h (owner drops one level, q_drop, t_vac), and riding on a parent project is already the Fs path and PW4. There is no 01 evidence for the take-over. Lowest priority under the 5-item cap.

dropped.behaviour: Run 4 #1 (orphan deferral, q_staff_defer_orphan) and run 4 #4 (w_wait_window), run 1 #4 (p_bundle_wait), run 2 #2 (sw_cycle_only), run 3 #3 (p_hold_to_cycle)
dropped.reason: Duplicates, merged into kept item 3 (p_hold_to_cycle). Run 4 #1's 'ask for resubmittal' part was merged into kept item 2.

dropped.behaviour: Run 3 #2 readiness haircut on q_veto (theta_ready_haircut)
dropped.reason: Duplicate, merged into kept item 2 (a staff-stage screen conditional on vacancy). Its batch-shrink part overlaps the already-covered a_sg017 range and the dropped f_aps_thin.

kept.behaviour: Partial award with descope. When the gap after design is larger than the top-up that can be found, staff recommend funding only part of the batch. The sites with the largest overrun (new conduit or curb ramps) are dropped until the gap fits. Dropped sites go back to the pool as deferred, not TERMINATED, and can return at a later cycle.
kept.parameter: q_partial: probability that staff recommend a partial award instead of the current all-or-nothing q_topup draw. Sites are dropped in descending order of per-site overrun. Dropped sites re-enter the pending pool after t_reentry.
kept.range: q_partial U(0, 0.8), with 0 as the control (the current F-f rule). t_reentry U(6, 24) months. Optional: the next 5YPP window (2027 autumn to 2028) is the earliest re-entry point.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f gap branch (q_topup, else TERMINATED) and the TERMINATED rule in D3.4. Today F-f has only a binary draw. D3.1 delta_split covers splitting only at application time, and the partial funding in D3.3 is for HSIP only.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3. l.185: allocation is 'based on the application package prepared and submitted by the eligible applicant', reviewed by SFCTA staff, then CAC, then board (SP p.22). This shows staff shape what reaches the board. l.179-180 and l.613: the 5YPP is about 202% ahead of pay-as-you-go, with $0 to $0.5M per year uncommitted, so a full top-up is often impossible. l.184: the strategic plan cut projects to 85-89%, a precedent for trimming scope to fit money. No document shows APS sites being descoped after design. Two runs cite '13th St +$2.7M, 01 §2.11' as a precedent: §2.11 (l.369-379) has no such figure, and grep finds no $2.7M anywhere in 01. That precedent exists only in 02 F-f's own citation and could not be verified.

kept.behaviour: Reprogramming inside EP17. Staff cover the overrun by moving money from another EP17 line (most likely the SG017 hardware-replacement row, or a line that is slipping) through a minor or 5YPP amendment, before any new-money top-up is considered. This is a zero-sum transfer: the donor line's work slips.
kept.parameter: q_reprog: probability that an intra-EP17 transfer is offered and used for an overrun. The amount is capped at min(gap, a_reprog), and the transfer takes t_reprog.
kept.range: q_reprog U(0, 0.6), with 0 as the control. a_reprog U($0, $0.5M) per year, matching the uncommitted headroom in 01 l.613. If the donor is SG017, a_reprog must share one budget with PW6's a_sg017 so no dollar is counted twice. t_reprog 3-4 months (Lincoln Way precedent).
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f: a new funding step between 'within contingency' and the q_topup draw. It interacts with PW6 (q_sg017_block, a_sg017). This is not covered: PW6 uses SG017 at allocation time, F-k is the director 10% / SG000 reserve, and F-j is a board veto of the amendment that opens the local line.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. l.179: committed $27.49M against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202% ahead; FY26-28 lines are hardware replacement $0.5M/yr and visibility $0.4M/yr. l.613: uncommitted headroom $0 to $0.5M/yr, 'only by changing the hardware replacement row or amending the 5YPP', which directly supports the donor-row route. l.177: Lincoln Way 5YPP revision took 3-4 months. l.447: SG017 FY25-26 $1M went to controller replacement, and FY27-28 use is unknown. l.176: failure-driven projects get EP17 money first, so donor slack competes with them. No document shows staff using reprogramming for an overrun.

kept.behaviour: Timing the top-up to a window. Staff advise holding the overrun request and folding it into the next 5YPP (starts 2027 autumn, adopted 2028) instead of a stand-alone request now. While the project waits, costpress keeps raising cost, and the 12-month commitment clock applies.
kept.parameter: p_wait_5ypp: probability that staff steer the first top-up request to the next 5YPP cycle. If chosen, the q_topup draw waits until the 5YPP adoption date. If not, it uses the normal allocation lead time.
kept.range: p_wait_5ypp U(0, 0.6), with 0 as the control. The wait runs to the 2028 adoption date, about 12-24 months. Do not add an approval boost dq: no source supports it, so keep dq = 0 or run it only as a labelled sensitivity.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f top-up timing, interacting with costpress (M-C1) and the 12-month commitment rule in D3.4. Not covered: F-e's t_pause applies only after a denial in the contracting-out branch, and F-j's 'wait for next 5YPP' applies only to opening the local line.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3. l.192: the next strategic plan and 5YPP start 2027 autumn and are adopted 2028 (SP p.8, p.10, p.46). l.193: 8-13 weeks from application to allocation, no August meeting. l.183: construction allocations must be committed within 12 months. l.180: 'the next five years are not expected to see this level of advance'. No document shows staff deliberately delaying a request.

kept.behaviour: Staff-stage review delay and conditions loop. A top-up cannot be decided at once: it goes through the allocation calendar (8-13 weeks, no August meeting) and staff, then CAC, then the board. Staff may ask for a revised estimate or schedule, which adds resubmission rounds before the board sees the item.
kept.parameter: n_cond: number of staff-requested resubmission rounds before the board decision. Each round adds t_round, on top of the fixed calendar lead time.
kept.range: n_cond in {0, 1, 2} (weights drawn from a Dirichlet); t_round U(1, 3) months. The base lead time is 8-13 weeks and requests are pushed past August. The control is n_cond = 0 with zero lead time (the current behaviour).
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f (and F-e) q_topup draw: adds a pre-decision delay. The event table in O3 gains a top-up decision event on the allocation calendar. Not covered: O3 has no local allocation calendar, and F-j models only a board veto or deferral.
kept.evidence: The calendar part is document-supported: 01 l.193 gives 8-13 weeks with no August meeting (allocation-request-calendar 2025/2026 p.1), and l.185 gives the staff → CAC → board chain (SP p.22). The conditions loop has no document support. One run also cited 01 l.319 for a 'seek your own sources first' condition. That line is SFMTA's duty under the 2007 settlement (SA07 §IV.A.1), not an SFCTA allocation condition, so it does not support an SFCTA condition and was dropped.

kept.behaviour: Precedent-dependent top-ups. Approval chances for a later top-up depend on how many top-ups were already granted in the same 5YPP period, through precedent caution or a finite discretionary pool. This creates order effects across overrunning projects.
kept.parameter: phi: q_topup(n) = q_topup0 × (1 − phi)^n_prior, where n_prior is the number of top-ups granted in the current 5YPP cycle, reset each cycle.
kept.range: phi U(-0.2, 0.4) (negative means approval gets easier after a precedent), with 0 as the control (independent draws).
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f and F-e, and the q_topup row in D10 (currently U(0, 0.7), drawn independently each time with no memory).
kept.evidence: No document support. The 13th St $2.7M top-up that the runs cite as 01 §2.11 is not in 01: §2.11 at l.369-379 has no top-up, and grep finds no $2.7M. Only 02 F-f's own citation names it. Even the direction of the effect is unknown, so the range spans both signs.

dropped.behaviour: Run 3: fold the APS overrun into a larger EP18 or corridor host project, so the gap is paid from the host budget and the sites follow the host schedule (q_host, sw_absorb).
dropped.reason: Only one run proposed it, and it fell below the cap of 5. The model already has most of it: the 'merge into existing project' route in D3.4 and the partner-risk logic in F-g / PW1. Moving an already-designed stand-alone batch into a host project has no source. 01 l.168-170, l.378 and l.409 support corridor projects as a path for APS in general, not as a way to absorb overruns.

dropped.behaviour: Run 3: q_divert, where the sponsor is redirected to seek HSIP or SS4A match funds first.
dropped.reason: It is a second mechanism inside one proposal, so it cannot be one parameter together with n_cond. Falling back to other funds is already covered by the path fallback chains in D3.6 (PW1/PW6 → amendment → general fund → HSIP) and by F-k.

dropped.behaviour: Run 1: condition that SFMTA must first try its own sources before SFCTA tops up.
dropped.reason: The cited evidence was misread. 01 l.319 is SFMTA's duty to seek funds under the 2007 settlement (SA07 §IV.A.1), not an SFCTA allocation condition. No source supports the condition.

dropped.behaviour: Run 4: dq, a higher approval probability after a deliberate hold.
dropped.reason: No source supports it. It was merged into the kept p_wait_5ypp item, with dq held at 0, or run only as a labelled sensitivity.

dropped.behaviour: Run 1: N_pool form of a shared discretionary top-up pool.
dropped.reason: It duplicates the precedent effect and was merged into the kept phi item, a single parameter with the same effect.

kept.behaviour: Post-approval claw-back after an outage: once a dedicated APS line exists, a visible controller-failure or outage event lets staff and board reprogram its unallocated balance to controller or hardware replacement through a routine 5YPP amendment, so a won amendment can lose its money before installs.
kept.parameter: q_claw (share of the APS line's unallocated balance reprogrammed per outage event), driven by exogenous lambda_outage (events per year)
kept.range: q_claw U(0, 0.6); lambda_outage U(0.1, 0.5)/yr (two events, 2022 and 2025, in about four years)
kept.rule_modified: New failure path F-n between F-j success and D3.4 delivery: at each outage event, cut the PW2 line's unallocated A_local balance by q_claw. 02 has no outage event (grep for outage/停电 finds nothing), and q_sg017_block (PW6, D10 l.375) only blocks SG017 before a request is made.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3 l.176: 'controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages' (OCT25 p.7). 01 itself tags this 【推断】. 01 §2.1 l.126 【事实】: EP17 hardware replacement $1M (FY25+FY26) went to about 98 controllers, although PIF 2023 had listed APS replacement as an eligible use. 01 l.446 【事实】: the SG017 CIP scope covers both APS and hardware. No document shows money being taken back from an approved APS line.

kept.behaviour: Staff screening before the board: SFCTA programming staff do not docket a standalone amendment. They tell the sponsor to come back with a ready package, or fold the request into the 2027-28 5YPP update. Because the board never votes, no veto is recorded, and the delay is longer than t_defer.
kept.parameter: q_screen (probability staff do not forward the amendment in this cycle); if screened, the request waits until the next 5YPP window or for t_screen months
kept.range: q_screen U(0, 0.5) (0 reproduces the current model); t_screen U(3, 18) months, capped at the 2027-autumn to 2028 update
kept.rule_modified: Adds a pre-board filter in D3.5 F-j and in D3.6 PW2 (and in the PW6 'amendment' fallback) before the q_veto draw. The θ_defer clock runs from submission. Run 3's readiness gate (strain(t) or specified = 0 triggers a hold) is merged here as one possible trigger.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3. l.185 【事实】 (SP p.22): allocation is based on an application package from a qualified applicant, and the order is SFCTA staff, then CAC, then board. l.186 【事实】: readiness carries weight 5 of 31. l.181 【事实】: Signal Shop staffing is often the limiting factor. l.192 【事实】: the next strategic plan and 5YPP start in autumn 2027 and pass in 2028. No document shows staff declining to docket a request.

kept.behaviour: Offset requirement: approval is fund-neutral. The APS line is paid for by an equal cut to another EP17 line, most likely SG017 hardware replacement, the line that carries outage-driven controller money. The APS gain is then paid for by a higher chance that controller-replacement and SG017-APS requests go unfunded.
kept.parameter: sw_offset (0/1) with share_offset (fraction of the APS line taken from SG017 when the switch is on)
kept.range: sw_offset in {0, 1}, default 0; share_offset U(0, 1)
kept.rule_modified: Couples the outcome of D3.5 F-j / D3.6 PW2 to D10: when sw_offset = 1, lower a_sg017 by share_offset × A_local and raise q_sg017_block to match. At present PW6 treats SG017 as a fixed $500k per year, independent of the amendment.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3 l.179 【事实】 (EP17-5YPP p.10-11, p.14): $27.49M committed against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202% ahead. FY26-28 has about $2.80M a year, all assigned, including hardware replacement at $0.5M a year, and there is no APS row. l.613 (tagged 【推断】): uncommitted headroom of $0-0.5M a year, available 'only by changing the hardware-replacement line or revising the 5YPP'. No document records an offset rule.

kept.behaviour: Leverage-contingent release: staff recommend the restored APS line only as local match. Prop L money is released only after SFMTA wins an outside grant (HSIP, SS4A or ATP), which ties PW2 to the success of the federal pathway.
kept.parameter: sw_leverage_gate (0/1): the first PW2 allocation waits for an awarded outside application
kept.range: {0, 1}, default 0. When the switch is on, the wait follows the existing HSIP cycle timing (C13 award 2027-03/04, C14 2029). If the grant is lost, the line stays dormant until the next cycle.
kept.rule_modified: D3.6 PW2: gate A_local release on PW1 (HSIP) award. Today PW1-PW6 are independent branches, linked only by fallbacks after a rejection.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01. §2.3 l.186 【事实】: 5YPP scoring gives leverage 4 points. §2.4 l.240 【事实】: Prop L was used as a 20% match, $1.4M of $7M, for the federal SS4A Tenderloin (Larkin) signal project. No document shows staff making an APS line conditional on a grant.

kept.behaviour: Out-year programming: the approved APS line is placed in FY28/29 or later because near-term pay-as-you-go cash is already committed. Approval is not the same as money that can be allocated now.
kept.parameter: delta_prog (months from amendment approval to the earliest allowed allocation request)
kept.range: U(0, 30) months; 0 reproduces the current model
kept.rule_modified: Entry of the D3.4 local batch: design starts at approval + delta_prog. This is separate from F-j's t_defer, which delays the vote, not the money. Measure θ_defer and θ_idle from approval, so a back-loaded line can trigger an early switch to the general fund or HSIP.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.3. l.179 【事实】: FY26-28 is fully assigned. l.180 【事实】 (EP17-5YPP p.11): 'the next five years are not expected to be this far ahead.' l.194 【推断】: pay-as-you-go from FY28/29 on is about $2.0-2.8M a year. No document records a programming-year decision for APS.

dropped.behaviour: Partial or haircut approval: the board passes the amendment, but the APS line is sized at a fraction phi of the request (phi_haircut, phi_cond, a_cap, phi_amend; runs 1, 2, 3, 4)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D10 A_local (02 l.358). When the dedicated line is open, A_local = U(0.5M, 2M) × APS share U(0, 0.5), so the draw already spans token lines down to about $0. A second multiplier would shrink the same quantity twice. The new part, a fund-neutral offset (run 3 sw_neutral, run 4 f_offset), is kept separately as the offset requirement.

dropped.behaviour: Staff redirect the request into existing PW4 (bundled corridor) or PW6 (SG017 scope) routes instead of restoring the line (run 3, q_redirect)
dropped.reason: Covered by D3.6. PW6 is already the SG017-scope route with no 5YPP revision (02 l.245), and PW4 bundles APS with parent projects. The redirect switches between pathways the model already compares, so it adds no new rule.

dropped.behaviour: Tranche allocation: design-only first grant, construction money after 95% design, and lapse under the 12-month rule (run 4)
dropped.reason: Proposed by one run only, and dropped to stay within five kept items. D3.4 (02 l.205) already makes the local batch finish design (t_des) before installs. The 95%-design and 12-month rules (01 l.182) are facts, but no document shows them applied to APS. The proposal needs three parameters (f_tranche, t_tranche, q_lapse), not one.

dropped.behaviour: Outage raises q_veto for the next amendment vote (part of run 2's outage proposal)
dropped.reason: Merged into the claw-back item. A separate change to q_veto would need a second parameter and has no source.

kept.behaviour: Conditional / split / tranched approval. Staff recommend the SG017 allocation, but the new-APS share is ring-fenced or capped, and released only after a condition is met (a named site list with pole/conduit adequacy, or the controller work done first). If the condition is not met by a deadline, the unspent APS share goes back to controllers. This is a third outcome between 'APS allowed' and 'blocked'.
kept.parameter: q_cond (probability a non-blocked SG017 grant carries an APS condition) + t_cond (release lag, months); on a miss past t_cond_deadline the APS share reverts to controllers
kept.range: q_cond U(0.1, 0.8) (union of run ranges 0.1–0.6 / 0.2–0.8 / 0.2–0.7); t_cond U(3, 12) months; reversion deadline U(6, 24) months; optional cap a_aps_ring U(0, 0.5) of the line; all inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.6 PW6 (l.245) and §D10 q_sg017_block / a_sg017 (l.375): the grant draw gets a third 'conditioned' branch; the effective a_sg017 arrives after t_cond and can revert
kept.evidence: Not covered: 02 has only the binary q_sg017_block plus the a_sg017 cap, with no lag or reversion; F-j (l.229) applies only to amendments. Citations checked: 01 l.185 [fact]: awards are 'based on the application package' and go staff, then CAC, then board. 01 l.181 [fact]: Signal Shop staffing is 'often the limiting factor'. 01 l.447 [fact]: FY25–26 $1M went to about 98 controllers. 01 l.446 [fact]: the CIP condition text 'where … conduits and poles are in satisfactory condition'. Run 1 also cites 01 l.354 for the Signal Shop, but that line is the PROWAG rule, so the citation is wrong (the correct line is l.181). No document shows SFCTA attaching a condition to an SG017 allocation.

kept.behaviour: Pre-submission steering / redirect. Before or during drafting, staff signal that new APS does not belong in SG017 ('replace' only). They point SFMTA to a 5YPP amendment or the 2027–28 5YPP, or SFMTA quietly leaves APS out. No rejection is ever recorded, so in the event stream the funder's block looks like the applicant's choice.
kept.parameter: p_steer (probability that a PW6 attempt is deflected before submission) + fallback switch {amendment PW2 now, wait for the 2028 5YPP}; the agent loses D_prep / t_steer months
kept.range: p_steer U(0.1, 0.6); t_steer U(0, 4) months; P(fallback = next 5YPP) U(0, 0.6), with the wait fixed to the 2028 adoption date; inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.6 PW6 entry, before SUBMITTED (l.245), and the F-j fallback choice (l.229). In a steered run this replaces the allocation-stage q_sg017_block draw. It can also be written as a funder-signal term in the §D3.1 p_start logit (l.133) for the PW6 task only
kept.evidence: Not covered: q_sg017_block acts at allocation, F-j after an amendment is filed, and p_deflect (l.124, l.342) is A2's own buck-passing, not the funder's. Citations checked: 01 l.446 [fact]: CIP allows new APS, but the 5YPP description says only 'replace'. 01 l.613 [inference]: headroom ~$0.5M/yr can change 'only via the hardware row or a 5YPP amendment'. 01 l.185 [fact]: SFCTA acts only on submitted applications. 01 l.83 [inference]: the 'no money / no application' loop. 01 l.192 [fact]: next 5YPP starts autumn 2027 and is adopted in 2028. Steering itself has no source.

kept.behaviour: Failure-driven, time-varying crowd-out. SG017 money goes to controllers whenever a visible failure or security finding appears, so the APS share can be taken back mid-cycle. The block probability therefore depends on fault events (or on the size of the controller backlog), not on one static draw.
kept.parameter: lambda_fault (visible-fault events per year; each event takes back fraction f_take of the unspent APS share and raises q_sg017_block)
kept.range: lambda_fault U(0.1, 0.6)/yr; f_take U(0.3, 1.0); alternative backlog form q_block = q_lo U(0.1, 0.3) if backlog cleared, otherwise q_hi U(0.6, 0.9); inferred from 2 events in about 4 years
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D10 q_sg017_block / a_sg017 (l.375), changed from a per-run static draw to an event process; new exogenous event in O3 (l.70)
kept.evidence: Partly covered: the D10 l.375 definition already names 'used up by failure-priority projects', but only as a static U(0.2, 0.9) draw. Kept as a refinement. Citations checked: 01 l.176: controllers got EP17 hardware money after the 2022 and 2025 outages (OCT25 p.7), tagged [inference] in 01. 01 l.126 / l.447 [fact]: $1M went to about 98 firewall-defect controllers. 01 l.69 [inference]: money moves only for visible faults. 01 l.179 [fact]: 202% over-programmed. The backlog stock and clearing rate (run 1) have no source.

kept.behaviour: Eligible-site filter at grant time. Staff fund SG017 APS only at sites that already have a documented pole/conduit adequacy check (readiness), or that are co-located with a controller or hardware job in the same allocation. The PW6-eligible C-type set shrinks to that fraction, so SG017 APS money can go unused even when there is no block.
kept.parameter: f_elig (share of C-type backlog sites eligible for SG017 APS at grant time: surveyed and/or co-located); optional survey task t_survey that uses K_crew
kept.range: f_elig U(0.05, 0.7) (run ranges: f_surveyed 0.1–0.7, rho_overlap 0.05–0.5); t_survey U(2, 9) months per batch; inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.6 PW6 eligibility filter (l.245), applied before the a_sg017 cap; links to K_crew / strain (§D3.4 l.205, M-B)
kept.evidence: Partly covered: PW6 limits SG017 to C-type sites with usable poles/conduit, drawn as facts, but needs no documented check and has no co-location term. Citations checked: 01 l.186 [fact]: 5YPP scoring gives readiness 5 and leverage 4. 01 l.446 [fact]: the 'satisfactory condition' condition with no site list. 01 l.126 [fact]: the 2023 PIF made APS replacement an eligible use. 01 l.181 [fact]: Signal Shop limit. Neither the survey requirement nor the co-location rule has a source. Merges run 3 (survey gate) and run 2 (co-location).

kept.behaviour: Cash-flow placement. Because EP17 is about 202% over-programmed against pay-as-you-go, staff approve the allocation but put the APS share's reimbursement in a later fiscal year. The money exists on paper but cannot be spent until later, which squeezes installs before the 2028 5YPP reset.
kept.parameter: t_cash (months between grant date and earliest spend date for the SG017 APS share)
kept.range: t_cash U(0, 18) months; optional s_cash U(0, 0.6) share moved to the later FY; inferred
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.6 PW6 (l.245) and §D3.4 delivery start (l.205): earliest spend of SG017 APS money = grant date + t_cash
kept.evidence: Not covered: D10 treats FY27/FY28 $500k as spendable when granted. t_defer (l.229, l.381) delays only the amendment vote. Citations checked: 01 l.179 [fact]: $27.49M programmed against $8.52M pay-as-you-go, about 202%. 01 l.180 [fact]: 'the next five years are not expected to be over-programmed to this degree'. These support the cash pressure, not the staff tactic itself.

dropped.behaviour: Pilot-as-precedent feedback (run 4): a delivered SG017 APS batch lowers later q_sg017_block / q_veto, and a late one raises them
dropped.reason: It cannot be written as one parameter: it needs a per-channel precedent counter plus two coefficients. Its feedback rests on no evidence: the D4 Lincoln Way case (01 l.177) is a timing precedent, not proof that delivery lowers later refusals. It was also the weakest proposal, so it was cut to stay within the 5-item cap.

dropped.behaviour: Slack reallocation inside EP17 (run 4): strain-driven underspend in other EP17 lines moved to APS
dropped.reason: The rules already cover it. 01 l.613 says headroom can change only via the hardware row or a 5YPP amendment, so this is either the existing uncommitted headroom $0–0.5M/yr (02 O2 l.64, A_local) or a PW2/F-j amendment. The run itself flagged it as borderline. The strain×underspend coupling has no source.

dropped.behaviour: Separate duplicates merged
dropped.reason: Into 'Conditional approval': run 1#1, run 2#1, run 3#1 and run 4#1. Into 'Pre-submission steering': run 1#2, run 2#4, run 3#2 and run 4#3 (5YPP redirect). Into 'Failure-driven crowd-out': run 1#3 (backlog) and run 2#3 (fault events). Into 'Eligible-site filter': run 3#4 (survey) and run 2#5 (co-location).

kept.behaviour: Deadline-gated bundling request: MOD/MDC staff ask SFMTA (the applicant, not Caltrans) to fold the SG142 APS scope into the SG015 SI02 carrier application instead of filing APS-only. It counts for the current window only if it lands before the package freezes. Otherwise it carries over as a bump to the next window (C14). With the C13 deadline one week out and D_prep U(1,6) months (02 D10 l.344), the model gives almost no C13 effect, so in practice this is a C14 lever. Caveat: QA13 Q32/Q68 say HSIP ranks by BCR only and support letters are for reference only, so a letter aimed at Caltrans would do nothing.
kept.parameter: q_letter_bundle: added probability that a PREPARING (or newly started) HSIP task builds the carrier+APS bundled instance (the PW1 start move) from PW0. Applied once when the staff action fires (p_letter per window), only if lead time >= D_prep + (m-1)*delta_split. Otherwise it is stored as a carry-over bump gamma_carry to the next window.
kept.range: p_letter U(0, 0.5); q_letter_bundle U(0, 0.3); gamma_carry U(0, 1); default off (0), matching zero observed APS letters
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 task state machine (PREPARING packaging choice / p_start). Lets the D3.6 PW1 start occur endogenously from PW0.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.279 (advisory-only tools; 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters both on curb ramps; 0 APS letters); l.283 (ODA staff proposed follow-up with MTA/DPW and a support-letter recommendation, follow-up not observed); l.309 (2026-09-18 agenda has no APS item); l.311 (MDC activation rule unknown, test at zero and non-zero); l.420 (SG142 as written ineligible, only a carrier BCR application could qualify); l.442 (SG015 and SG142 on separate lines, both funded from HSIP C13 EST). No document shows a staff request changing the packaging.

kept.behaviour: Window-aware timing and abstention: staff hold advocacy in a window that can no longer be made eligible in time, and concentrate it in a lead period before the next window opens, instead of applying pressure at random times.
kept.parameter: sw_window_aware (0/1). When on, the yearly pressure events (lambda_press) are rescheduled to t_lead months before the next HSIP or local window opens, and suppressed when time-to-deadline < D_prep.
kept.range: t_lead U(3, 12) months; off = current Poisson timing (control)
kept.rule_modified: Timing of the pressure events that feed pressure(t) in D3.1 (O3 event schedule). The logit coefficients are unchanged. Distinct from F-m (D3.5 l.232), which generates exogenous silence.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.290 (MDC channel inferred at about one letter/resolution a year); l.224 (CIP carried SG136 with HSIP C12 money but no SF APS application among the 330 C12 applications), consistent with action arriving too late or never; the 2.4 C13 deadline row. No document shows deliberate waiting. Run 2's carry-over idea overlaps and is folded into the first item.

kept.behaviour: Reframe into the curb-ramp / ADA public right-of-way pipeline: staff steer the request away from 'APS' toward accessible pedestrian infrastructure, so APS rides with ramp work that has a federal schedule duty and a funded general-fund line. The cost is dilution and delay from DPW coordination.
kept.parameter: sw_ramp_route (0/1) with r_ramp: share of APS backlog intersections that become fundable on the ramp/ADA line, arriving after delay t_ramp
kept.range: r_ramp U(0, 0.4); t_ramp U(6, 36) months; off = 0
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 / PW4 funding-source assignment: a new routing row. Today ramps appear only as the q_ramp cost add-on (D10 l.357) and the general fund appears only as a late fallback in PW1/PW2/PW6.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.281 (MOD co-funded and ranked DPW ramps under the 2008 ADA transition plan, which entered the capital plan); l.284 (ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) schedule duty, and no APS equivalent was found in the materials read; the comparison itself is labelled inference); l.282 (ODA said the ramp budget 'will rise sharply' and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate); l.257 (general-fund ADA public right-of-way $55M FY26-30); l.258 (mayor's budget lists curb ramps and barrier removal as a priority); l.279 (both letters went to ramps). No source shows ramp money being used for APS.

kept.behaviour: Non-adversarial compliance reframe: a staff memo or hearing item cites the NYC federal court order and ADA exposure to turn the agency's answer from 'no money' into 'what is the cheapest eligible vehicle'. There is no lawsuit and no D1 tier change. Run 3's 'list APS in the transition plan with a dated target' is a stronger variant of the same idea (enforce floor), so it is folded in here.
kept.parameter: delta_reframe: multiplicative cut in p_deflect for t_reframe months after a reframe event (events at rate lambda_reframe)
kept.range: delta_reframe U(0, 0.4); t_reframe U(3, 12) months; lambda_reframe U(0, 1)/yr; 0 = control
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect, D10 l.342 U(0.5,0.95)). Sits below the D1 escalation tiers and the PW3 structured-negotiation step, and leaves enforce(t) untouched.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.282 (ODA deputy director explained NYC's speed by its federal court order and asked DPW/MTA to coordinate); l.131 (author's first-hand account of deflection responses: 'no money', 'very expensive'); l.283 (follow-up proposed, not observed). No source shows a reframe lowering deflection.

kept.behaviour: Equity-priority site insertion: MOD hands SFMTA disability-priority intersections to name in the HSIP carrier package even when they are low-crash. Because packing is by BCR, this can dilute the package below 5.0 (F-a) or below the cut-off (F-b). It is an advocacy feedback that can hurt funding.
kept.parameter: n_equity: number of forced low-BCR intersections inserted ahead of the BCR sort, applied with probability p_equity per package
kept.range: n_equity in {0,1,2,3}; p_equity U(0, 0.4); 0 = control
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 route A packing algorithm steps 2-3 (frozen BCR-descending order with a stop when package BCR < 5.0); outcomes F-a / F-b
kept.evidence: Verified in 01: l.280 (MOD supplies a 'city public project' site list for APS scoring, TOOL p.8, but that feeds A1's request scoring, not HSIP packing); l.172 (EP26 equity priority names people with disabilities, $47M, EP p.13-14, a Prop L context, not HSIP); 2.4 decision rule 'only BCR ranks' (QA13 Q32, Q68). No document shows MOD pushing sites into an HSIP package.

dropped.behaviour: Coalition seeding toward Caltrans for an HSIP rule change (p_rule_relax) (run 1)
dropped.reason: Excluded on purpose: 02 D3.3 l.199 says the model has no 'rule relaxation' switch because there is no landable rule, and D11 lists 'pure-APS rule relaxation' as not modelled. The citations are real (01 l.207 advisory-committee reply 'will study again'; l.221 C10 Mission Viejo), but re-adding it would reverse a frozen decision.

dropped.behaviour: Shared yearly attention slot: the letter goes to ramps instead of APS (a_ramp) (run 2)
dropped.reason: The model has no ramp-decision event, so the trigger cannot be evaluated and the rule collapses to lambda_press×(1−a_ramp). That is already absorbed by the lambda_press U(0,0.5) prior (02 D10) plus F-m (D3.5 l.232). The citations do check out (01 l.279, l.284, l.287).

dropped.behaviour: MDC support letter aimed at the Prop L amendment, lowering q_veto / t_defer in F-j (run 3)

kept.range: p_letter U(0, 0.6), baseline 0 reproduces the observed 2024-26 absence; eps_letter U(0, 0.5), where 0 means no effect. Applies to F-j only. HSIP is excluded because support letters do not count there (01 line 215).

kept.range: ask_scale U(0.2, 1.0), where 1.0 is the current model; gamma U(0.5, 2.0) (inferred). The A_local draw for the open line (02 line 358) is scaled by ask_scale. It is not a separate budget.

It also cuts against the evidence: 01 line 356 records that the Access Board deleted the PROWAG provision under which replacing a controller or software would trigger APS. tau in 02 (D3.2 line 150, D10 line 355) is about poles and conduit, not controllers. The claim about controller money after outages (01 line 176) is itself marked inference.

dropped.reason: No source, and it adds a second parameter on top of p_hold. The proposal itself says there is no document support. Only the hold that the proponent starts was kept.

kept.behaviour: Ramp-cost re-attribution. MOD staff reframe the over-plan new-conduit and curb-ramp lines as ADA transition-plan (curb-ramp) work, not APS work. They push to have that share charged to the DPW curb-ramp programme (or the General Fund ADA right-of-way line), so the APS batch only has to cover the APS hardware remainder. The cost is still counted once; only the payer changes.
kept.parameter: phi_ramp_shift: the share of the ramp/conduit-tagged part of the F-f gap above contingency that moves to the ramp budget. Two helpers go with it: q_ramp_shift, the probability the ramp programme accepts, and t_ramp_wait, the extra delay from ramp-programme sequencing. Both are reported on the cost_by_actor Public Works line.
kept.range: phi_ramp_shift U(0, 0.5), default 0 = current model (runs proposed 0–1). q_ramp_shift U(0, 0.6). t_ramp_wait U(1, 18) months. All inferred.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f: the gap is resolved in this order: contingency (κ_cont), then ramp shift, then q_topup, then TERMINATED. The D3.4 delivery start for affected sites is delayed by t_ramp_wait. A Public Works line is added to cost_by_actor (D4). Not covered now: F-f sends the whole gap to q_topup, D10 l.357 treats q_pipe/q_ramp only as cost add-ons, and 02 never mentions DPW.
kept.evidence: The premises are verified in 01. l.281: MOD co-funded and ranked the DPW curb ramps in 2008 (transition plan p.3). l.284: ramps carry a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) timetable duty that APS lacks. l.282: the ODA deputy asked DPW and MTA to coordinate. l.279: both MDC letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) were about ramps. l.117: excavation triggers ramp work. l.257: the $125M/10y GF ADA right-of-way money flows to ramps. l.373: the ramp line grows from $4.0M to $8.1M/$12.2M. One counter-point: l.376 says DPW ramp construction does not trigger APS ('APS is MTA's business'), so DPW may refuse the shift. No document shows a shift like this ever happening, and nothing says what share could legally be moved.

kept.behaviour: Event-triggered advocacy aimed at the top-up decision. When the overrun is discovered or a top-up is pending, MOD staff use the MDC's roughly once-a-year slot to put the case on the agenda and draft a support letter or resolution to the budget body. This raises the chance that this one project gets its top-up. In the current model, pressure arrives at a fixed exogenous rate and does not depend on project events.
kept.parameter: d_qtopup_letter: an additive boost to q_topup while a letter is active. Its trigger is p_react, the probability that an F-f gap produces a letter, gated by the next MDC meeting after lag t_meet. The boost lasts or decays over k_letter months.
kept.range: d_qtopup_letter U(0, 0.3), clipped so q_topup ≤ 1, default 0. p_react U(0, 0.5) (01 s2.8 suggests low activity). t_meet U(0, 3) months. k_letter about 6 months. At most 1–2 escalations per year.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f (and F-e) top-up draw: q_topup becomes min(1, q_topup + d_qtopup_letter) for the affected project only. Optionally the letter also adds one pulse to pressure(t) in D3.1. Not covered now: λ_press (D10 l.340) is exogenous, pressure(t) only enters p_start (D3.1 l.133), and q_topup (l.379) is flat.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01. l.73: MDC/ODA have advisory tools only (resolutions, hearings, support letters), about 1 chance a year, and the activation rule is unknown. l.279: the letters go to CPC and so far have been about ramps only, none about APS. l.283: ODA staff proposed a follow-up and support letter after 2026-07-17. l.311: activation is an unknown parameter, tested at zero and non-zero. Correction to run 1: 01 says the letters go to CPC; nothing documents letters to the SFCTA or SFMTA Board. No document shows an APS letter or any effect of a letter on a top-up.

kept.behaviour: Strategic timing of the top-up ask. Instead of asking at once and risking the one-shot q_topup draw ending in TERMINATED, staff hold the overrun request (and the letter supporting it) until the next capital budget, Prop L allocation or ramp-line appropriation window. Sites without an overrun go ahead in the meantime.
kept.parameter: sw_wait_window (switch). It comes with t_window_gap, the months to the next window taken from the budget calendar, and d_qtopup_window, the boost to q_topup when the ask is filed inside a window.
kept.range: sw_wait_window ∈ {0, 1}, 0 = current model. t_window_gap U(0, 24) months. d_qtopup_window U(0, 0.25). Inferred.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f: a wait branch is added before the q_topup draw. The over-budget site holds (it is not TERMINATED) until the window and then draws q_topup + d_qtopup_window. Its siblings without an overrun are unaffected (F-f already acts per site). Not covered now: F-f has a single immediate draw, F-e's t_pause applies only to the outsourcing differential, and F-j's t_defer applies only to the Prop L amendment.
kept.evidence: Only the calendar facts are documented. 01 l.373: the ramp lines step up in FY27/28. 01 l.256–258: the GF ADA allocation and the mayor's capital priority on ramps. 02 F-j: precedents of a 3–4 month Prop L amendment. No document shows MOD or MDC timing a request to a budget window, and no document shows that in-window asks succeed more often.

kept.behaviour: Standing down after a deflection. After SFMTA answers with 'high cost / no funding', MOD/ODA staff accept the promise and do not do the follow-up they proposed. The MDC channel then stays quiet. This quiet is caused by the agency's answer, unlike the random interruptions in F-m.
kept.parameter: p_followup: the probability that a real follow-up happens after a DEFLECTED event. If it does not, the MDC share of pressure is zero for t_wait months.
kept.range: p_followup U(0, 0.6), default 0.3; p_followup = 1 gives the active-follow-up control. t_wait U(3, 12) months.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (l.123: currently 'this pressure leaves no effect' and nothing more) and F-m. With probability 1 − p_followup, a deflection also starts a quiet spell of the MDC pressure channel. F-m's λ_quiet is random and does not depend on the agency's answer, so this coupling is new.
kept.evidence: One documented instance in 01. l.130: in 2026-07 SFMTA answered the MDC with 3 pages on 'Technical Challenges & Cost' ($40k–$1.5M, ~$200k each for conduit and ramp). l.283: ODA staff proposed a follow-up with MTA/DPW and support-letter recommendations ('follow-up not observed'). The 2.7.1 row for 2026-09-18 says the agenda, the ODA report and the LightHouse brief had no APS item and no letter. l.287: no public comment at the 2026-07-17 item. Caveat: l.288 says the 2026-09-18 page returns 404, but 2.7.1 does contain that meeting's agenda, so cite 2.7.1, not l.288. This is a single case (n=1); the size of p_followup is not documented.

kept.behaviour: Raising legal exposure when the batch stalls. When the only funded APS batch stalls on an overrun above contingency (no top-up, TERMINATED pending), MOD staff or the Council pass it to the city attorney or ADA coordinator as a litigation-risk item. This raises perceived enforcement without the PW3 negotiation → lawsuit ladder.
kept.parameter: eps_flag: a jump in enforce(t) at a stall event, decaying over k months. It fires with probability p_flag.
kept.range: eps_flag U(0, 0.3), default 0. p_flag U(0, 0.3). Decay is the same as the k used for pressure. Inferred.
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.1 p_start (the β_enf·enforce(t) term, l.133) and optionally q_topup in F-f. A stall event (an F-f gap left unfunded) adds eps_flag to enforce(t). Not covered now: enforce(t) only moves by the ε_enf annual rate (l.395) or through PW3 (l.243).
kept.evidence: Verified in 01. l.112: the SFMTA senior engineer names the 'litigation environment' as a reason for doing curbs together. l.282: the ODA deputy explained NYC's speed by a federal court order. l.92: outside enforcement is a possibly large multiplier with an unknown rate in SF. No document shows MOD flagging an APS overrun as a legal risk, or any such channel.
