kept.behaviour: Window-timed APS support letter. The office uses its roughly one letter or resolution a year on APS, either as a stand-alone letter or as an APS line on the annual curb-ramp letter to CPC. It times the letter to a local funding decision: the Prop L EP17 amendment (F-j), the general-fund biennial request (PW2), or the SG017 allocation (PW6). Today that slot always goes to ramps.
kept.parameter: p_letter_APS: per-year probability that the annual MDC letter or resolution names APS. Companions: delta_letter, subtracted from q_veto (F-j) and from P(general-fund request not listed), active only if the letter lands within t_align months before the decision.
kept.range: p_letter_APS U(0, 0.6)/yr, 0 = current model (observed value 0 in 2025-26); delta_letter U(0, 0.25); t_align U(0, 6) months. No effect on HSIP.
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto becomes letter-dependent instead of a fixed prior) and the D3.6 PW2 signpost 'general fund not listed'. Add an annual MDC letter event to O3, dated in April, inside the local Jan–Jun preparation window. Not covered: 02 has MDC only inside C2's generic λ_press.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.7 row 1: the tools are only advisory (resolutions, hearings, support letters to CPC), and the 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters were both for curb ramps, with 0 APS letters. §2.7 last row says 'about 1 letter/resolution per year' (labelled inference). §2.7 also records ODA staff promising after 2026-07-17 to come back with a support-letter suggestion (not observed afterwards). The budget deadline '5-01 of even years' is verified in 01 §3.1. Caveat from 01 §1.1 (Caltrans row): support letters do not score in HSIP, so the effect must stay on local lines only. No document shows that an APS letter would ever be sent or would change a vote. Run 4 cited line numbers (287, 291) that drift by about 4 lines, but the content is real.

kept.behaviour: Follow-up promise as a pressure sink. When advocates press at the council and SFMTA answers 'costly, no money', the office or SFMTA offers a follow-up or a soft commitment ('we will follow up with MTA and DPW', 'will study'). The pressure is treated as handled and advocates stand down, but the follow-up never reaches an agenda.
kept.parameter: p_absorb: probability that a non-deflected MDC-channel pressure event goes into a follow-up channel instead of pressure(t). Companions: t_followup, the stand-down months; q_letter_after, a small chance the follow-up ends in a real letter.
kept.range: p_absorb U(0, 0.7), 0 = current model; t_followup U(2, 12) months; q_letter_after U(0, 0.4)
kept.rule_modified: D3.1, the (1 − p_deflect) pressure branch, for MDC-channel events only: split it into a pressure(t) increment and an absorbed part. F-m (D3.5) gets a second, endogenous trigger next to the random hazard λ_quiet. Only partly covered: F-m quiet periods are random and independent of what any actor said.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.7, ODA staff row: after 2026-07-17 they proposed to 'follow up with MTA and DPW … then propose recommendations and a support letter', labelled fact with 'follow-up not observed'. 01 §2.7.1, row 2026-09-18: the agenda, ODA report and LightHouse presentation contain no APS item and no support letter, two months after the promise. 01 §2.7.1 also says this means only 'not observed within the searched range', not zero activity. Run 2's soft-commitment variant cites 01 §2.4 (Caltrans advisory committee: 'HSIP does not fund APS-only projects', 'will study again'); that citation is verified but concerns another agency. Advocates standing down as a result is inference.

kept.behaviour: Turn the 'costly / no money' reply into a tracked record. After the meeting, the office files a written request or a minuted action item asking SFMTA for a per-intersection funding-status and cost table for the ~76 intersections (funded / source / not applied for, with C-type versus N-type costs). A vague answer becomes harder to give, and a refusal becomes a visible event.
kept.parameter: q_followup: probability that a written or minuted follow-up is filed and delivered after a council pressure event. On success: an oversight pulse delta_ov that decays over T_ov, and p_deflect multiplied by d_defl for the next 2r months.
kept.range: q_followup U(0, 0.6), 0 = current model; delta_ov U(0, 0.3), oversight capped at 1; T_ov U(3, 18) months; d_defl U(0.6, 1.0) (floor p_deflect at 0.1)
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch: replace 'this pressure leaves no effect' with 'with probability q_followup add the oversight pulse and scale p_deflect'. oversight changes from a static prior (D10 U(0.05, 0.6)) to prior + decaying pulse, and enters p_start through β_ov. Applies only to M-A and M-D, where p_deflect > 0. Only partly covered: PW3 raises oversight only as an outside package. Shares its trigger with the follow-up-sink item above, so code the two as branches of one event.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.1, response-pattern row: the 2026-07 MDC presentation spends 3 pages on 'Technical Challenges & Cost' ($40k–$1.5M; pipe and ramp about $200k each) and says the remaining request-list intersections are 'selected based on funding', with no per-site reasons. 01 §1.2 has the 'say no money / no application' loop with no actor able to force an application. Run 3's cost-split rebuttal cites 01 §1.1 (peer row: $10k–76k packaged, $52–65k NYC), verified; it is merged here as another trigger for the same p_deflect reduction. No document shows any such request being filed.

kept.behaviour: Reframe APS as an ADA transition-plan item. The office argues that APS belongs in the City's ADA transition plan or its general-fund ADA public right-of-way line, as curb ramps already do, and asks for a dated APS line (count or percent by year). This turns an optional safety request into a compliance-style item with a named schedule.
kept.parameter: p_reframe: per-year probability that a dated APS line is added to the transition or capital plan. Companions: specified set to 1 for t_plan-lagged t_ada months, plus an optional source share s_ada of the ADA right-of-way line added to A_local.
kept.range: p_reframe U(0, 0.3)/yr, 0 = current model; t_plan U(6, 24) months; t_ada U(6, 36) months; s_ada U(0, 0.05) of the ADA right-of-way line (inferred fraction; 0 = schedule only, no money)
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 p_start (β_spec·specified switched on without a full PW3 start); D10 A_local (an optional new source term). Leaves the D3.3 HSIP rules unchanged. Only partly covered: PW3 sets specified only as an outside accountability package, and no route goes through a city-side plan update.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.7: ramps carry a federal transition-plan schedule duty (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)), while in the materials read APS has none (the comparison is labelled inference). §2.7: MOD (2008) co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps, which entered the 10-year capital plan. §2.7: the 2006-03 resolution targeted 25% by 2010, and the outcome was 116 (about 9–10%). 01 §2.6: the general-fund ADA public right-of-way line is $55M (FY26-30) + $71M (FY31-35), and CP-T p.11 says accessibility capital is 'usually reflected in other departments' budgets, including transport and signals (APS)'. No document shows the office attempting this reframing. s_ada is invented.

kept.behaviour: Ramp-hosted APS. Instead of arguing APS as a stand-alone SFMTA cost, the office uses its co-ranking role in the DPW curb-ramp programme. When a scheduled ramp job touches a listed signalised intersection, APS is added to the same dig and the ramp budget carries the ramp and pipe share, so SFMTA's stated cost drivers are paid elsewhere.
kept.parameter: p_ramp_link: probability that a DPW ramp job at a pending listed intersection carries APS. Companions: lambda_ramp, the rate of ramp jobs at pending intersections; f_shared, the share of the q_pipe/q_ramp cost paid by the ramp budget.
kept.range: p_ramp_link U(0, 0.6), 0 = current model; lambda_ramp U(0.02, 0.1)/yr per pending intersection; f_shared U(0, 1); delay t_ramp_host U(6, 36) months
kept.rule_modified: D3.4: add a 'ramp-hosted' delivery row that enters the internal queue under K_crew. The cost of hosted intersections is reduced by f_shared·($200k pipe + $200k ramp), and the rest is booked as extra budget in cost_by_actor. Add a PW7 row in D3.6 beside PW5. Not covered: PW4/Fs cover SFMTA signal projects only, and ramps appear in 02 only as the cost item q_ramp.
kept.evidence: Verified in 01 §2.7: MOD (2008) co-funds and ranks DPW curb ramps, and the ODA deputy said the ramp budget 'will go up a lot' and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate strategy. 01 §2.1: APS digging triggers ramp work, pipe and ramp are about $200k each, and the senior engineer says not touching existing ramps is about '5× faster'. Against it, 01 §1.1 (Public Works row) records as fact that ramp construction does not trigger APS today. Whether ramp or ADA money may legally pay for APS has no document.

dropped.behaviour: Steering the MOD 'city public project' site list to move some of the ~76 up the queue (run 1)
dropped.reason: The lever is real (01 §2.7, TOOL p.8), but editing the list under pressure has no document. It also does not change how much money flows: HSIP ordering in D3.3 is by BCR and tier, so a score bonus cannot act there, and it would only reshuffle never_served. Lowest priority under the 5-item cap.

dropped.behaviour: Quiet legal-exposure briefing to city lawyers that multiplies ε_enf (run 4)
dropped.reason: Mostly covered by D1 enforcement tiers, ε_enf (D10) and PW3's escalation path. The briefing itself has no document, and 01 §2.7 notes that APS has no federal retrofit schedule duty, which weakens the lever (κ_legal ≈ 1 is plausible). One run only; over the cap.

dropped.behaviour: Accepting a symbolic or partial SFMTA answer to close the issue (run 2, q_accept)
dropped.reason: Not dropped as a behaviour. It is merged into the 'follow-up promise as a pressure sink' item (same effect: pressure cut and F-m-like quiet tied to a promise) and counted in its runs_proposing.

dropped.behaviour: Cost-claim rebuttal by splitting the 76 into cheap C-type and costly N-type (run 3)
dropped.reason: Merged into the 'tracked record' item. It acts on the same rule (p_deflect lowered after an office action), and its citation (01 §1.1 peer costs) was verified.

dropped.behaviour: Window-aligned pressure: holding pressure events until a budget or capital-plan window (run 3)
dropped.reason: Merged into the window-timed APS letter item. The 'within t_align of a decision' timing is the same mechanism, and the April letter dates are verified in 01 §2.7.

kept.behaviour: Drafting-window scope ask. While SFMTA is drafting the SG017 allocation request (task in PREPARING), MOD/ODA staff send a staff-to-staff ask, or a Council support letter, asking that the request text name new APS at C-type intersections with adequate poles and conduit, citing the CIP scope text. A late ask has no effect.
kept.parameter: p_scope_ask: probability per SG017 request cycle that the ask lands inside the PREPARING window, U(0, 0.6), 0 = status quo. Effect when it fires: q_sg017_block × (1 − η_scope), with η_scope U(0, 0.5).
kept.range: p_scope_ask U(0, 0.6); η_scope U(0, 0.5). Both are inferred.
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.6 PW6 signpost (the q_sg017_block draw, §D10 l.375), drawn when the SG017 task enters PREPARING (§D3.1). It is not covered: PW6 treats q_sg017_block as exogenous, and pressure(t) is untimed and only feeds p_start. Note that q_sg017_block bundles two causes: SFCTA limiting the scope to 'replace', and the money going to failure-priority controllers. The ask plausibly moves only the first, which is why η_scope is capped at 0.5.
kept.evidence: The cited lines exist and say what is claimed. 01 l.279: the two MDC letters (2025-04, 2026-04-16) both went to curb ramps, and there is no APS letter. 01 l.283: ODA staff proposed after 2026-07-17 to follow up with MTA and DPW and then recommend support letters (no follow-up observed). 01 l.309: the 2026-09-18 agenda has no APS item and no letter. 01 l.446: the SG017 CIP scope text allows new APS where conduits and poles are satisfactory. 01 l.447: the FY24 allocation went to cabinets, detectors and RRFB, and FY25–26 went to about 98 controllers. No document shows a wording ask ever being made. Run 3 cited '02 lines 446-447', but the text is in 01.

kept.behaviour: Folding APS into the curb-ramp track. MOD, which co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps under the ADA transition plan, asks that a pending crossing whose ramp is being rebuilt get APS in the same work order. APS then rides on a track that has a federal timetable, and it shares the excavation cost.
kept.parameter: q_ramp_pair: probability per pending C crossing per year that a ramp rebuild is converted into a ramp + APS work item through MOD coordination. A paired crossing drops the q_ramp $200k add-on and inherits the parent delay t_parent.
kept.range: U(0, 0.15) per crossing per year (inferred). 0 = status quo, since DPW currently does not trigger APS.
kept.rule_modified: Adds a ramp-event generator to the 02 §D3.4 delivery routes, next to the 'merged into existing project' row and PW5's λ_hw generator. It modifies the q_ramp cost add-on (§D10). It is not covered: D3.4 and Fs only bundle with signal works, and no route can be triggered by a ramp event or by a non-SFMTA actor.
kept.evidence: Verified. 01 l.281: MOD (2008) co-funded and ranked the DPW curb ramps under the ADA transition plan. 01 l.282: the ODA deputy said the ramp budget 'will rise sharply' and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate. 01 l.284: ramps have a 28 CFR 35.150(d)(2) timetable, and APS has none (the comparison is labelled an inference in 01). 01 l.376: DPW leaves room for future APS, but ramp work does not trigger APS ('MTA's job'). 01 l.118: pipe about $200k, ramp about $200k. 01 l.112: the senior engineer cites the litigation environment as the reason to insist on doing the curbs together. The 'five times faster' claim is at l.126, not l.127 as run 4 cited. No document shows MOD actually asking for this pairing. Run 1's extra gain_ramp_link multiplier was dropped (one parameter only).

kept.behaviour: On-record accountability ask. MOD/Council asks SFMTA, through a Council status item or a records request, for a written public answer on why the SG017 request does or does not include new APS where the CIP scope allows it. This makes the 'cost / no funding' deflection costly. It does not ask for money.
kept.parameter: d_pdefl: multiplier on p_deflect for the SG017 task for r to 2r months after a documented ask, U(0.5, 1). The ask fires with probability q_ask per request cycle, U(0, 0.4).
kept.range: d_pdefl U(0.5, 1); q_ask U(0, 0.4). Both are inferred.
kept.rule_modified: The 02 §D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect, r) for the Prop L EP17 / SG017 task. It is not covered: PW3 (§D3.6) raises owner/specified/oversight as an outside policy intervention, and no actor-triggered event changes p_deflect.
kept.evidence: Verified. 01 l.129: SFMTA's 2026-07 MDC presentation answered with cost ($40k–$1.5M) and 'selected based on funding'. 01 l.130: author first-hand account that oversight does not work and the parties pass the buck. 01 l.83: the 'no money / no one applied' closed loop (01 itself labels the loop an inference). 01 l.446: the CIP scope allows new APS. Run 2 cited l.131, but the line is l.130. No document shows a records request or a status item. Run 3's 'redirect deflected pressure to the funder' targets the same DEFLECTED branch but is a separate behaviour; it is listed under dropped.

kept.behaviour: Strategic waiting. Because SG017 money visibly goes to a failure-priority item (the firewall controllers), MOD/Council deliberately hold the APS ask during that SG017 cycle so they do not spend about one influence slot a year on a likely loss. They release the held pressure as a burst at the next 5YPP rewrite or HSIP window.
kept.parameter: sw_strategic_wait (switch). When on, λ_press = 0 during an SG017 PREPARING window in which a controller-priority signal is present, and λ_press × g_burst at the next 5YPP (2027 autumn – 2028) or HSIP window.
kept.range: sw_strategic_wait in {0, 1}; g_burst U(1, 4) (inferred)
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.5 F-m (quiet period) and λ_press (§D10). It replaces the exogenous λ_quiet draw with a quiet period conditioned on the window. It is only partly covered: F-m quiet periods are random, not tied to SG017 or to a later release.
kept.evidence: Verified. 01 l.447: the FY25–26 SG017 $1M went to about 98 controllers with a firewall vulnerability. 01 l.290: MDC channel, 0 binding force, about one letter or resolution a year (labelled an inference in 01). 01 l.73: the activation rule is unknown. No document shows a deliberate decision to hold back, so the behaviour itself is an inference.

kept.behaviour: Site-list supply. MOD hands SFMTA a ready list of pole-and-conduit-adequate C intersections drawn from its 'city public projects' site list, so the SG017 request can name APS sites with less preparation work.
kept.parameter: d_prep_offset: months removed from D_prep for the SG017 instance when MOD supplies a list, floored at 0.5·D_prep. It fires with probability p_list per cycle.
kept.range: d_prep_offset U(0, 2) months; p_list U(0, 0.4). Both are inferred.
kept.rule_modified: 02 §D3.1 preparation time D_prep + (m − 1)·δ_split (D_prep in §D10). It is not covered: D_prep is exogenous, and no outside actor can offload preparation work.
kept.evidence: Verified. 01 l.280: MOD supplies the 'city public projects' site list used in APS scoring (TOOL p.8). 01 l.106: one associate engineer scores all applications. 01 l.118: pipe and ramp add-ons of about $200k each, so site choice drives cost (run 3 cited this as about l.119). No document shows MOD offering a list for SG017.

dropped.behaviour: Meeting-calendar gating of Council pressure (run 1 #2) and window-dependent g_hi/g_lo rates on λ_press (run 3 #3, timing part)
dropped.reason: The citations check out: 01 l.287–288 (zero public speakers on 2026-07-17; next meeting 2026-09-18), l.307 (APS on the agenda twice in 2018–26), l.309. But the proposal needs three parameters (p_agenda, q_slot_lost, t_meet). For the SG017 question its effect is already captured by the per-cycle probability that the scope ask lands inside the window (kept item 1). The window-dependent rate overlaps with strategic waiting (kept item 4).

dropped.behaviour: Cross-issue linkage: Council support for other SFMTA items made conditional on a named APS line (run 1 #4)
dropped.reason: No document support; it is pure inference (the run says so itself). It acts on the same hook as the kept scope ask, so the model could not tell the two apart.

dropped.behaviour: Redirecting deflected pressure to the SFCTA board, Mayor's budget staff or CPC (run 3 #4)
dropped.reason: Proposed by one run only, and it needs three parameters (p_redirect, beta_fund, k_f). The funder-side specified/oversight uplift overlaps with 02 §D3.6 PW3. The actor-triggered action on the DEFLECTED branch is kept in narrower form as the on-record accountability ask. The citations are real (01 l.83, l.130 rather than l.131, l.283), but nothing documents the behaviour.

dropped.behaviour: Run 1's gain_ramp_link pressure-efficiency multiplier on the ramp channel
dropped.reason: A second parameter on top of the ramp pairing, with no source for its size. The ramp behaviour is kept as the single parameter q_ramp_pair.

kept.behaviour: Venue shift: while the APS owner post is vacant, the advocacy organisation sends part of its pressure past the empty SFMTA desk to funder-level nodes (the SFCTA board for a Prop L EP17 amendment, the general-fund/budget route, the elected level). The ask becomes 'fund an APS line' rather than 'apply'. There is a trade-off: pressure on A2 shrinks by the same share.
kept.parameter: phi_redirect (share of pressure events routed to funder nodes while owner is vacant). It enters F-j with fixed scaling: q_veto × (1 − 0.5·phi), t_defer × (1 − 0.3·phi).
kept.range: U(0, 0.7). 0 = the current model. Active only while F-h is vacant (and the F-i freeze is on); reverts to 0 when the post is filled.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure branch (pressure_A2 vs pressure_upstream) and F-j (q_veto, t_defer). Optionally F-k q_dir. Checked: 02 has no rule where pressure acts on q_veto, t_defer or q_dir. F-j/F-k are exogenous draws, PW2 is designer-started, and DEFLECTED only resets the task to IDLE after r months.
kept.evidence: Verified 01 §2.8 l.320: SA07 §IV.J.2 and §V say plaintiffs take 'meaningful participation' in Prop K applications and support SFMTA's requests to the mayor and council, so this upstream channel is part of the historical repertoire. Verified 01 §2.3 l.177: the D4 supervisor used NTP $500k and a 3–4 month 5YPP amendment. Verified l.188: the CAC has advice-only power. Verified 01 §2.8 l.329: no 2024–26 public advocacy statements on SF APS funding were found. No document shows advocates re-targeting during a vacancy.

kept.behaviour: Advocate-supplied preparation (external steward). During the vacancy the organisation and its legal partners keep the pending-request tracker. They also assemble the ranked intersection list, crash and site data and support letters, and hand a near-ready package to the capital-budget staff (A2). This adds outside preparation labour, not pressure.
kept.parameter: f_aid (fractional cut in D_prep, and in the F-h q_drop abort chance, for a PREPARING task while owner is vacant)
kept.range: U(0, 0.5), 0 = current model. Activation chance per window p_aid U(0, 0.5), or simply a switch. At most one field at a time.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 PREPARING duration D_prep + (m−1)·δ_split and the q_drop clause of F-h. Checked: D_prep is an exogenous U(1, 6); F-h only drops owner and applies q_drop; C2 only emits pressure (O2 actor table).
kept.evidence: Verified 01 §2.8 l.320: SA07 §IV.J.2 gives a 'meaningful participation' right in funding applications. Verified l.321: semiannual reports must include 'funds SFMTA applied for and status' and 'efforts to obtain Caltrans funds', so advocates hold the information. Verified 01 §2.7 l.281: MOD co-funded and ranked DPW curb ramps in 2008. Verified l.283: ODA offered to follow up and suggest support letters. Verified 01 §2.1 l.106: one associate engineer scores all requests. Run 3's Portland citation (11 community requests) is real but sits in §2.12 l.390, not §2.9. No document shows an advocate drafting APS application material in SF.

kept.behaviour: Calendar-timed pressure. The advocate holds back and concentrates its asks in the months just before a decision window (HSIP call, Prop L/5YPP cycle, budget). It does not press at a constant rate, and total annual pressure stays the same. This tests whether timing alone changes how often pressure meets an open window with an owner present.
kept.parameter: w_sync (share of annual pressure events moved into the months before each window opens; λ_press total unchanged)
kept.range: U(0, 0.8), 0 = current constant-rate model. Burst span 1–6 months before the window opens.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 pressure arrival process and D10 λ_press, interacting with the O3 window schedule and with F-m. Checked: λ_press is a constant Poisson rate (×2 only at PW3 start), F-m is a random quiet period, and k is pure decay. Nothing ties pressure to windows.
kept.evidence: Verified 01 §2.7 l.281 and §2.7.1 l.309: ODA said after 2026-07-17 it would come back with a support-letter recommendation, and the 2026-09-18 agenda, ODA report and LightHouse briefing had no APS item. Run 2 misdescribes 09-18 as an 'information item'; APS was in fact absent. Verified 01 §2.7 l.285: the 2026-07-17 meeting had 0 public comment. Verified 01 §5 l.624: the activation rate is unknown. No document shows deliberate timing. The extra assumption that p_deflect falls inside a burst is pure inference, so it is left out of the kept parameter.

kept.behaviour: Vacancy-contingent escalation or restraint. Once the advocate learns that the owner post is empty under a freeze, it changes its pressure rate. It may escalate (a demand letter citing the expired 2007 funding-seeking duty or ADA access) or deliberately hold back until a hire, so as not to waste pressure on an empty desk.
kept.parameter: m_vac (multiplier on λ_press, and optionally on ε_enf, while owner is vacant, after a notice lag of up to one semiannual report cycle)
kept.range: m_vac in {0.3, 1, 2, 4}, 1 = current model; values below 1 are restraint. Notice lag t_notice U(0, 6) months.
kept.rule_modified: D10 λ_press (and ε_enf / D1 tier step). This couples F-h to pressure(t) and enforce(t) in D3.1 p_start. Checked: in the baseline, vacancy affects only owner/q_drop; PW3's escalation follows a θ_idle policy signpost, not advocate response to vacancy; F-m is independent of A2 state.
kept.evidence: Verified 01 §2.8 l.318–319: a semiannual APS report still arrives, and LightHouse says it got the report re-established, restored 2022-07 (an advocate reacting to an information lapse). Verified l.321: SA07 §IV.A.1 contains the funding-seeking duty. Verified l.323: the agreement expired 2010-06-30. Verified 01 §2.8 l.333 and §5 l.624: the activation rate is unknown; test 0 and non-zero. Verified 01 §2.10 l.351: the NYC 2024 amended order requires 'full effort to secure funds'. Verified 01 §2.1 l.112: the senior engineer cites the litigation environment. No document shows SF advocates reacting to a staffing gap.

kept.behaviour: Ramp-rider reframing. The advocate joins the curb-ramp / ADA transition-plan coalition and asks for 'APS wherever ramps are rebuilt'. APS then rides a funding stream that has a federal timetable and recurring MDC support letters, and none of it goes through the vacant APS owner.
kept.parameter: p_ramp_rider (chance per ramp-rebuild funding event that an eligible C-class pending intersection gets APS as a funded add-on)
kept.range: U(0, 0.4), 0 = current model. Optional yearly cap on add-on cost b_ramp U($0, $200k). Cost uses the existing u0.
kept.rule_modified: New arrival path into D3.4 concurrent delivery (Fs → I), as a sibling of the PW5 λ_hw/b_hw generation rule, plus a row in D3.2. Checked: PW5 covers only button/hardware-change events and PW4 only parent projects. Both are owned by SFMTA staff, and q_ramp appears only as a cost add-on, so no ramp-program carrier exists.
kept.evidence: Verified 01 §2.7 l.278: the 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 MDC letters both concern curb ramps; no APS letter. Verified l.283: ramps have a federal transition-plan timetable (28 CFR 35.150(d)(2)), and APS has no corresponding obligation (the comparison is tagged 推断). Verified l.281: ODA said ramp budgets 'will rise sharply' and asked DPW and MTA to coordinate. Verified 01 §2.1 l.112 and l.123: the senior engineer insists on co-installing with ramps; 'installing with existing work is cheapest' (MDC23 p.6, MDC26 p.7). No document shows the advocate pursuing this route.

dropped.behaviour: Freeze-waiver campaign: the advocate seeks an essential-post exemption so the vacant post is refilled sooner (p_waiver hazard on t_vac). Run 1.
dropped.reason: Largely covered by the parameter sweep. F-h already draws t_vac U(3, 18) months and F-i draws strain_end, so the short-vacancy outcome that a waiver produces is already sampled. Proposed by only 1 run, and it would sit below the 5-item cap. Its citations check out: 01 l.105 shows the eligible list of 41 passed during the freeze; l.583 gives 6–9 months to fill; l.584 says freezes apply to 'non-essential' hiring.

dropped.behaviour: Settling for a procedural substitute (verbal promise, meeting, report), with trust loss and faster escalation if the promise lapses. Run 2.
dropped.reason: It cannot be written as one parameter or switch: it needs q_accept, a trust state tau_trust and m_lapse on ε_enf together. The one-off bump to oversight/specified overlaps PW3, and the pause overlaps F-m (t_quiet). Proposed by only 1 run, with no document support for the behaviour; 01 l.324 (MDC23 slide 10, 'only consulted') is tagged 推断.

dropped.behaviour: Refill pulse / withholding until hire (hold_frac, pulse_mult, w_wait). Runs 1 (cautious variant), 3 and 4.
dropped.reason: Merged, not kept separately. The restraint during vacancy is folded into m_vac < 1 in the vacancy-escalation item. The window-timing part is folded into w_sync. A separate release pulse at refill would need a second parameter.

kept.behaviour: Deadline-synchronised pressure: the advocate concentrates letters, meeting requests and testimony in the weeks before a known window deadline (HSIP C13 2026-11-02, Prop L / budget decisions) instead of applying pressure at a steady rate, so the pressure is present when the p_start draw for that window can still produce a SUBMIT.
kept.parameter: omega_window (sync multiplier on lambda_press inside the w months before each window deadline, with lambda_press scaled down elsewhere so the annual total is unchanged; omega = 1 reproduces the current model)
kept.range: omega in {1 (off), 2, 4} or U(1, 5); w U(1, 3) months
kept.rule_modified: Pressure-event arrival process feeding pressure(t) in the D3.1 p_start logistic (D10 lambda_press row); F-m quiet generator left as is
kept.evidence: Not covered: D10 lambda_press is a constant rate U(0, 0.5)/yr and pressure(t) decays with k; F-m quiet spells are random, not calendar-tied (02 l.232, l.340-341). 01 §2.8 l.332 and §5 l.624: no-event activation rate unknown, test 0 and non-zero (0.1-0.5/yr), verified. 01 l.330-331: 0/~39 board public comments on APS Aug-Oct 2026, no 2024-26 advocate statements found, verified. 01 l.323: LightHouse got the semiannual report re-established 2022-07, verified (shows targeted action, not deadline timing). No document shows advocates timing pressure to deadlines. Note for this situation: with one week left and D_prep U(1,6) months, a pulse now can only matter for C13 if the task is already PREPARING.

kept.behaviour: Advocacy at the local approval step: the advocate backs SFMTA's own local requests (Prop L EP17 amendment at the SFCTA board/CAC, top-up after overrun or contracting gap, general-fund request), including taking a deflected ask to the SFCTA venue named in the deflection, which makes local approval more likely.
kept.parameter: adv_local_lift (relative reduction of q_veto and t_defer, and relative increase of q_topup, applied while pressure(t) >= theta_press or while sw_ally = 1)
kept.range: adv_local_lift U(0, 0.3); 0 as control; switch sw_ally in {0,1}
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and F-e / F-f (q_topup), evaluated at the gap or amendment decision event
kept.evidence: Not covered: q_veto, t_defer, q_topup are fixed constants with no actor input (02 l.224-229, D10 l.379, l.381); D3.1 sends a deflected pressure to IDLE with 'no effect' (02 l.124). 01 l.320: SA07 §IV.J.2, §V, plaintiffs to participate in SFMTA's Prop K funding applications and support SFMTA requests to the mayor and council, verified, but the agreement expired 2010-06-30 (01 l.326) so it shows a past role, not current behaviour. 01 §2.3: D4 supervisor used NTP $500k for two new APS-equipped signals via a 5YPP amendment in 3-4 months, verified (supervisor-driven, not advocate-driven). 01 l.283: ODA proposed support-letter follow-up, not seen afterwards, verified. No 2024-26 document of advocates doing this.

kept.behaviour: Carrier-framed ask: instead of 'fund APS', the advocate asks for APS bundled with an eligible carrier (SG015 visibility upgrade, or a new countdown head SI18PB), relabelling the SG142 line, so the 'cost / no funding' reply is harder to give.
kept.parameter: delta_ask (relative cut in p_deflect for a pressure event that carries an eligible-shaped ask)
kept.range: delta_ask U(0, 0.6) (p_deflect becomes p_deflect × (1 − delta_ask)); switch sw_ask in {0,1}
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (p_deflect)
kept.evidence: Partly covered: p_deflect exists but is one constant per event, U(0.5, 0.95) (02 l.124, l.342). 01 l.130: SFMTA answered MDC with 3 pages of 'Technical Challenges & Cost' and 'selected based on funding', verified. 01 l.205: APS-only ineligible in any category (QA13 Q3), verified; 01 l.206: APS may go with a new countdown head SI18PB, verified. 01 l.420 and l.442: SG142 APS-only $488,144 ineligible in C13, while SG015 and SG142 are separate lines in the same C13 column, verified. No document of an advocate making such an ask or of its effect on deflection.

kept.behaviour: Pre-deadline package-scope ask: the advocate asks SFMTA, before the C13 submission, to add pending C-type intersections beyond the five named SG015 corridors to the carrier package (or pair SG142 intersections with SG015), so more APS rides on an eligible BCR application in C13 rather than waiting for C14.
kept.parameter: f_widen (share of non-corridor C-type intersections added to the C13 PW1 candidate set when the ask succeeds), with success probability p_scope_widen; no effect if the ask comes later than D_prep + (m−1)·delta_split before the deadline
kept.range: p_scope_widen U(0, 0.4); f_widen U(0, 0.5); 0 as control
kept.rule_modified: D3.3 packing step ① (candidate set; 'PW1 起手只限 SG015 走廊') and D3.6 PW1 start condition
kept.evidence: Partly covered: PW1 already bundles SG015 + APS in C13 but only on the five named corridors (~1 intersection) and widens to other corridors only in C14 after failure (02 l.241, l.192); the bundling itself is covered, only the C13 widening triggered by an ask is new. 01 l.444: SG015 scope limited to five named corridors, only Brotherhood/Lake Merced is an unfunded C on them, verified. 01 l.420, l.442: SG142 ineligible as written, same cycle as SG015, verified. 01 l.215: support letters not scored (QA13 Q32, Q68), verified. No document of an advocate making this ask. With the deadline one week out, the late-ask cutoff will usually bind.

kept.behaviour: District-supervisor NTP earmark: the advocate asks a district supervisor to put APS into an EP25 Neighborhood Transportation Program recommendation as a quick local source when SG142 fails in C13 or a pressure event is deflected.
kept.parameter: sw_ntp (0/1) with q_ntp, the yearly probability that a district earmark for APS is granted while advocacy pressure is active (grant size b_ntp and lag t_ntp drawn as attributes)
kept.range: q_ntp U(0, 0.3)/yr; b_ntp U($200k, $500k); t_ntp U(3, 6) months; sw_ntp in {0,1}
kept.rule_modified: New local-fund branch in D3.6 (between PW2 and the general-fund step) feeding the local batch rule (A_local) for the covered district intersections
kept.evidence: Not covered: 02 has no NTP / EP25 / supervisor rule (grep finds none); PW2 is only the EP17 amendment and F-k only the director's 10% / SG000. 01 §2.3: EP25 NTP $700k per district FY24-28 (NTP5 p.7-8), verified; D4 supervisor used NTP $500k to design two new signals with APS and passed the 5YPP amendment in 3-4 months (LW p.15-18), verified. The funding route is documented; that advocates trigger it is not (the precedent followed the 2024-11 Prop K vote, not an advocate ask).

dropped.behaviour: In-kind drafting help and nominations that cut D_prep / delta_split and force nominated intersections up the packing order (run 1; D_prep cut also in run 3's ask proposal)
dropped.reason: Weak mechanism and cut by the 5-item cap. HSIP ranks by BCR only and support letters are not scored (01 l.215), so what an advocate can supply (letters, narrative, nominations) does not shorten the engineering, crash and cost work SFMTA must do. Forcing low-crash nominations up the order conflicts with the frozen packing algorithm (02 l.192). The cited hook SA07 §IV.J.2 covers Prop K applications only and expired 2010-06-30 (01 l.320, l.326). Cited '01 §2.9 line 337' is a table separator; the 'selected based on funding' quote is at l.130.

dropped.behaviour: Ally-mode restraint / goodwill-triggered quiet, with escalation after failure (run 2; ally sign-flip part of run 1)
dropped.reason: Single run for the endogenous-pressure part; it needs two parameters (trust multiplier + escalate switch) and a new feedback rule. The approval-side effect of ally mode is merged into the kept 'adv_local_lift' item. Evidence (01 l.330-331, no 2024-26 statements) shows quiet but nothing on why. Cut by cap.

dropped.behaviour: Post-award watchdog shortening t_partner / t_con tails (run 1)
dropped.reason: Single run; no document of advocates acting on delivery dates; needs both an effect size and a budget split with start-side pressure (two parameters plus a reallocation rule). 01 l.321-323 (semiannual reports, 2022-07 restoration) verified but only shows reporting. Cut by cap.

dropped.behaviour: Venue switching of pressure across HSIP / Prop L / general fund after the ineligibility signal (run 3)
dropped.reason: Single run; 02 applies pressure(t) to each field's task without a per-field allocation, so this needs a new allocation structure plus a decay rule (gamma, w0), not one parameter. No document support for advocate venue choice. Cut by cap.

dropped.behaviour: Borrowed voice through MDC/ODA letter (run 3)
dropped.reason: Single run. Its 'already_in_model' claims are wrong: 02 D10 has no 'MDC activation' row and 02 does not state support-letter weight (that is 01 l.215). Facts cited from 01 (l.283 ODA proposal, l.309 no APS on 2026-09-18 agenda, l.276 letters only for curb ramps) verified. The effect is a one-off bump to oversight(t) or pressure(t), which the existing pressure-event mechanism already represents. Cut by cap.

dropped.behaviour: Package-content lobbying that forces the PW1 bundle in PW0/PW2/PW4 (run 2 as written)
dropped.reason: The bundling itself is already PW1's start rule (02 D3.6 l.241). The only new part, widening the C13 candidate set by an ask, is merged into the kept scope item.

kept.behaviour: Venue shift after a deflection: when SFMTA answers 'costly / no money' and points to SFCTA, the budget or Caltrans, advocates take the same ask to whoever holds the money (SFCTA board/CAC, a district supervisor's NTP allocation, Board of Supervisors budget). They ask for a named APS site or a named APS line, instead of dropping the ask.
kept.parameter: p_venue: probability that a DEFLECTED pressure event is re-routed to a funder or elected venue
kept.range: U(0, 0.6) per deflected event; 0 = current model (control). If it fires: a sponsored small local batch of 1-5 C-type sites, capped by the NTP $700k per district per 5 years, after a lag of U(2, 9) months, success U(0.1, 0.5). The re-routed share also enters funder-side pressure on the F-j draws.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch (adds a third exit beside 'returns to IDLE, no effect'). Adds a new NTP-type local route in O2/D3.6; 02 has no NTP rule today (grep: no NTP/EP25 in 02). Links to F-j and the PW2 start.
kept.evidence: Not covered by 02: D3.1 l.124 says the deflected pressure leaves no effect, and PW2 and F-j are started by SFMTA or the experimenter. Verified in 01: l.177 (§2.3), the D4 supervisor used NTP $500k to design two Lincoln Way signals with APS, and the 5YPP amendment took 3-4 months. l.171: EP25 NTP is $700k per district for FY24-28. l.124 (D3.1 in 02) and 01 l.130: deflection points to other bodies. l.320 (§2.8): SA07 §IV.J.2 gave plaintiffs a role in Prop K applications. Against the behaviour: l.330 (0 of ~39 board comments on APS) and l.331 (no 2024-26 advocate statements on SF APS funding). The channel is documented; advocates using it after a deflection is not.

kept.behaviour: Deflection ratchet and cost rebuttal: advocates put each 'costly / no money' reply on the record and answer the next one with SFMTA's own cost spread and peer unit costs. They then narrow the ask to a named, cheap list with a date. After that, a generic cost reply is less easy to give.
kept.parameter: rho_rebut: relative cut in p_deflect for each recorded deflection of the same field in the last 24 months
kept.range: U(0, 0.3) per prior deflection, floor at 0.3 x baseline p_deflect; 0 = current model. Optional companion: residual pressure kept after a deflection, U(0, 0.5); leave it out if only one parameter is allowed.
kept.rule_modified: D3.1 DEFLECTED branch and the p_deflect draw (D10 l.342: fixed U(0.5, 0.95)). Needs one counter per field. Flag for the author: this adds memory, against 02 l.91 'do not model learning'.
kept.evidence: Not covered by 02: p_deflect is one fixed draw (D10 l.342), and DEFLECTED leaves no effect (D3.1 l.124). Verified in 01: l.130 (§2.1), SFMTA's 2026-07 MDC talk gave a $40k minimum, a $1.5M maximum and about $200k each for conduit and curb ramps, and said the rest were 'selected based on funding'. l.392 and l.609: packaged California HSIP unit cost is $10.3k-76k. Correction: run 1 cites l.378 for this, but l.378 is Contract 35 at $0.3-1.07M per site. l.322: LightHouse says it got the semiannual report re-established in 2022-07. l.339: 90-day reply and 'likely within three years' duty (POL10). l.439: SG015 FY24 about $14k per site (this is §3.2, not §3.1). No document shows advocates using rebuttals.

kept.behaviour: Window-timed pressure: advocates concentrate their asks in the months before a known funding window (HSIP call deadline, the even-year budget submission, the 5YPP round) instead of spreading them evenly, because pressure outside a window decays before p_start is checked.
kept.parameter: w_sync: share of pressure events moved into the m_lead months before the next open window
kept.range: U(0, 1), or test {0, 0.5, 1}; m_lead fixed at 3 months (sensitivity U(1, 6)); annual lambda_press total held fixed; 0 = current Poisson timing
kept.rule_modified: O3 pressure-event generation (inter-arrival timing) and how it meets the window check in D3.1. D10 lambda_press and k are unchanged.
kept.evidence: Not covered by 02: lambda_press is a homogeneous Poisson rate with decay k U(1, 12) (D10 l.340-341). p_start is checked only when a window is open (D3.1 l.121). F-m (l.232) only switches pressure off at random. Verified windows in 01: l.219, HSIP C13 deadline 2026-11-02; l.192, 5YPP round starts autumn 2027 and is adopted in 2028; l.412, budget due before 5-01 in even years. No document shows advocates timing their asks. Run 2's data hand-off that shortens D_prep is a second parameter and was dropped.

kept.behaviour: Scope nomination at parent-project design: while a funded parent project (SS4A, corridor, new signal) is still in design, advocates name the pending intersections inside its footprint and ask for APS to be put in its scope.
kept.parameter: d_add: increase in the in-scope probability pi for a 'likely / unverified' merged intersection when an advocacy event lands during its parent's design window
kept.range: U(0, 0.3), capped at pi = 1; counts only during the parent's design months; 0 = current model
kept.rule_modified: D3.4 'merged into existing project' row (pi becomes pi + d_add x 1{event in design window}); one extra event type in O3; PW4 is unchanged
kept.evidence: Partly covered: D3.4 l.207 holds pi as a static probability, and PW4 (l.244) adds sites at design time only as an SFMTA routing choice. Verified in 01: l.455, Eddy/Fillmore, where the project says 12 of 16 sites include APS but this is not checked site by site; l.456, Golden Gate/Larkin; l.432-433, 13 corridor candidates and 52 sites with no identified parent. A related precedent no run cited: l.304, in 2010-10 LightHouse complained about Transbay APS placement and asked for design-stage involvement. That is about where APS goes, not about adding sites to scope. l.306 (2026-07 ODA follow-up) has no follow-up observed.

kept.behaviour: Coalition support at the second gate: advocates publicly back SFMTA's own request for APS money (a Prop L amendment, a general-fund line, a top-up) and bring in allied groups. The pressure changes from 'you must' to 'we will help you win the vote'.
kept.parameter: omega_support: relative cut in q_veto, t_defer and the q_topup shortfall in years when advocates are active
kept.range: U(0, 0.5), applied as q_veto x (1 - omega_support x 1{active}). 'Active' reuses the lambda_press / F-m state, so no new random process. 0 = current model.
kept.rule_modified: D3.5 F-j (q_veto, t_defer) and the q_topup draws in F-e/F-f; F-k q_dir optional
kept.evidence: Not covered by 02: F-j q_veto U(0, 0.5) and q_topup are exogenous (D3.5 l.229, l.224-225), and pressure enters only through p_start (D3.1). Verified in 01 l.320: SA07 §IV.J.2 and §V, plaintiffs support SFMTA's requests to the Mayor and Board. But the agreement expired on 2010-06-30 (l.324), and after 2010 plaintiffs are only consulted (l.326). l.177: the amendment precedent took 3-4 months. No evidence that support changes veto odds. This overlaps the support-letter part of run 4's venue-shift proposal, so that run is counted here too.

dropped.behaviour: Attention substitution across disability priorities (run 2): APS pressure falls while a rival item such as curb ramps is live (rho_sub)
dropped.reason: Already covered by D3.5 F-m (l.232) and D10 lambda_quiet / t_quiet: the model already switches lambda_press to 0 for spells. An exogenous rival calendar with a random duty cycle gives the same model behaviour as a random quiet spell, unless it is tied to windows, and that case is the window-timing item. The evidence is real (01 l.277: 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 letters were both on ramps; l.281: ramps have a federal timetable, APS none), so it is worth noting as the cause behind F-m, not as a new rule.

dropped.behaviour: Cheap escalation below litigation (run 4): a rights letter or administrative complaint bumps enforce(t) and lowers p_deflect
dropped.reason: Mostly covered by the D1 enforcement tiers and eps_enf, and PW3 already escalates to negotiation and then a lawsuit. It needs three parameters (p_complaint, b_complaint, a p_deflect cut), not one. The evidence weakens the hook: 01 l.281 says APS has no federal retrofit timetable.

dropped.behaviour: Ramp-programme bundling / coalition reframing (run 4): APS carried as an add-on in DPW curb-ramp jobs
dropped.reason: Covered in part by PW4 (merge into parent) and PW5 (add-on during hardware replacement, b_hw). It needs a switch plus two inferred probabilities. The cited channel goes against the mechanism: 01 l.376 says DPW leaves room for APS when designing ramps but ramp construction does not trigger APS, and APS is 'MTA's job'.

dropped.behaviour: Data hand-off that shortens D_prep (run 2, part of window-timed pressure)
dropped.reason: It is a second parameter (delta_data) beside the timing parameter, and has no source. It was removed when merging into the window-timing item.

kept.behaviour: Advocacy aimed at the top-up decision: once an overrun beyond contingency is known, the policy lead lobbies the funding bodies on that specific supplemental request (testimony, letters, calls to the district board member, a reminder of the 2007 duty to seek added funds, written support for the agency's request). The aim is to raise the approval odds of that one request, not to start new applications.
kept.parameter: beta_topup_adv: additive logit shift on q_topup (and on the single re-request after t_pause), applied only while the advocate is active (not in an F-m quiet spell) and a top-up request is pending
kept.range: U(0, 1.5) logit units; 0 = current model (control). The activation rule is unknown, so also scan P(advocate active at overrun) from 0.1 to 0.6
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f and F-e top-up draw: q_topup_eff = logistic(logit(q_topup) + beta_topup_adv * active(t)). The rules do not cover this today: pressure(t) enters only p_start (02 D3.1 l.133), q_topup is a fixed U(0, 0.7) prior (02 l.225, D10 l.379), and F-m (l.232) only gates whether pressure exists.
kept.evidence: Checked in 01 §2.8: l.319 SA07 §IV.A.1 duty to seek added funds; l.320 §IV.J.2 says plaintiffs take part 'meaningfully' in the Prop K applications and back SFMTA's requests to the mayor and council; l.321-322 semi-annual meetings and status reports; l.323 LightHouse says it got the report restored in 2022-07 (the advocate's own claim). 01 l.177 (§2.3): a D4 supervisor got a 5YPP amendment through in 3-4 months. Limits: the agreement expired 2010-06-30 (l.326). l.331 found no public advocacy on SF APS funding in 2024-26, and l.624 sets the no-event activation rate to 0. The '13th St $2.7M top-up' precedent cited by runs 1, 2 and 4 is NOT in 01: only 02 F-f claims it ('账本 §2.11'), and 01 §2.11 (l.369-379) has no such row. No document shows advocates acting at a top-up, and the effect size is unsourced.

kept.behaviour: Cost-line unbundling: the policy lead, in coalition with mobility-disability groups and the disability office, argues that the new curb ramps (and possibly the trenching) are ADA curb-ramp work. That share would then be charged to the citywide curb-ramp / ADA right-of-way general-fund line, leaving only APS hardware and conduit on the APS batch.
kept.parameter: s_ramp_shift: probability that the ramp add-on of an over-budget site is accepted by the curb-ramp program. Attached delay t_ramp_wait before APS install when the shift succeeds
kept.range: s_ramp_shift U(0, 0.5), 0 = control; amount shifted = the ramp add-on only (0 or ~$200k per site); t_ramp_wait U(2, 36) months
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f gap computation: insert a ramp-line step before the q_topup test. Also adds a fourth source route to PW4 (02 l.244) and a new payer in cost_by_actor (l.260). The rules do not cover this: PW4 routes are parent, corridor and local/SI02 only, and the ramp add-on is always charged to APS (02 l.51, l.357). Modelling caveat: in 02 the conduit and ramp add-ons are drawn at list entry and sit in planned cost, so the 'new ramps found at design' in this situation has no hook in the model as written. The shift has to act on the known q_ramp add-on, or the add-on discovery has to move to the design node.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.72 (overview table, not §2.6 as run 2 said): the general-fund ADA right-of-way earmark of $125M over 10 years flows to curb ramps, and APS has no matching earmark (inferred). l.257: $55M FY26-30 / $71M FY31-35. l.258: the mayor's budget lists priority curb ramps. l.373: ramps $4.0M in FY26, requests of $8.1M/$12.2M. l.279: MDC letters in 2025-04 and 2026-04-16 cover curb ramps only. l.282: ODA asked DPW and MTA to coordinate. l.281 (§2.7, not §2.10 as run 1 said): the 2008 transition plan co-funds DPW ramps. l.284: ramps carry a federal timetable duty and APS does not. l.374 and l.378: ramp delivery is slow (Contract 35 ~8 yrs; 6-9.5 yrs). Counter-evidence at l.376: DPW says ramp work does not trigger APS and APS 'is MTA's business'. No document shows ramp cost being moved off an APS project.

kept.behaviour: Triage inside an over-budget local batch: the advocate accepts a phased batch. Cheap, conduit-ready sites go first and the costliest sites are dropped or deferred, instead of letting a random or default site absorb the termination and stall the batch.
kept.parameter: sw_triage: switch for which sites F-f drops when the batch gap is unfunded (0 = default/unspecified order, 1 = costliest dropped first, cheapest kept)
kept.range: {0, 1}; 0 = control
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f termination step and the local-batch sizing (planned cost x (1 + κ_cont), l.225). Only part of this is new. Deferral is already covered: a TERMINATED site returns to the pool and can be repacked (02 D3.4 l.210 ④), so run 2's 'deferred instead of terminated' and run 1's option 2 add nothing. What is not written down is WHICH site is dropped inside a local batch; HSIP BCR ordering at D3.3 l.192 does not apply to local batches.
kept.evidence: Checked: 01 l.119 and l.130 (MDC26 p.4-6): costs run from $40k to $1.5M with conduit/ramp ~$200k each, so ranking by cost is feasible; l.130 says the rest of the request list is 'selected based on funding'. l.186: the 5YPP score weights community support 5. l.327: NFB and ACB differ on how much to concede. No document shows an advocate proposing phasing or reordering a funded batch. Run 3's ω_adv (advocate-priority ordering) would need a per-site priority flag that has no data source, so it is folded into this switch.

kept.behaviour: Phased descoping: the policy lead accepts (or resists) an APS-only minimal scope at over-budget sites where the existing pole, conduit or ramp is usable. The new ramp or conduit is deferred, so the site is kept rather than terminated.
kept.parameter: p_descope_keep: share of over-budget sites kept at APS-only scope (cost = c_base, the pipe/ramp add-ons removed) instead of TERMINATED
kept.range: U(0, 0.6) under 'accept'; 0 = control / 'resist'
kept.rule_modified: 02 D3.5 F-f: adds a third outcome between top-up and TERMINATED. The rules do not cover this: q_pipe and q_ramp add-ons are always charged (l.357), and PW6 (l.245) selects usable-pole sites only at entry and never downscopes after an overrun.
